findings.title: Registration data does not reach the assessor readiness surface
findings.summary: Registration data does not reach the assessor readiness surface. After completing every required Assessor Registration field, the Expertise tab reports 0 expertise areas, 0 specializations and no years of experience, and prompts "Add at least one area so clients can find you" — while displaying the registered industries in a separate row. A brand-new assessor is therefore immediately unready and undiscoverable despite having supplied the data.

findings.title: Duplicate industries are accepted
findings.summary: Duplicate industries are accepted. The same industry entered in two rows passes client and server validation and persists ("Technology · +1 more"). The qualification chips in the same form do dedupe, so the inconsistency is internal.

findings.title: Experience is not cross-validated against date of birth
findings.summary: Experience is not cross-validated against date of birth. "60 Years" was accepted for a 41-year-old and stored. With the 18+ rule enforced, no eligible user under ~78 can legitimately hold 60 years of experience, so a public credibility signal is unconstrained.

findings.title: Email verification gives no success confirmation — reproduced here on an Assessor identity (third occurrence overall)
findings.summary: Email verification gives no success confirmation — reproduced here on an Assessor identity (third occurrence overall).

findings.title: No warning before lockout
findings.summary: No warning before lockout. Attempts 1–4 give no attempts-remaining hint, so a user with a forgotten password locks themselves out without notice.

findings.title: lockout message enumerates accounts
findings.summary: The lockout message enumerates accounts. Five wrong-password attempts against any address reveal whether it belongs to a real account: an existing account returns "User account is locked!", while the pre-lock message is deliberately generic. This defeats the non-enumeration posture the login form otherwise maintains and contradicts an explicit requirement of ASS-001 step 2.

findings.title: No security notification of any kind is sent when an account is locked — no email and no in-app message
findings.summary: No security notification of any kind is sent when an account is locked — no email and no in-app message. The account holder is never informed that their account was locked out, which is the observable signature of a brute-force attempt against them.

findings.title: At 360×800 the role-change dialog's Cancel and Submit render outside the dialog's painted box and outside the viewport, with page scroll locked and…
findings.summary: At 360×800 the role-change dialog's Cancel and Submit render outside the dialog's painted box and outside the viewport, with page scroll locked and neither the dialog nor its container scrollable. Pointer and touch users cannot reach either action; only keyboard Tab recovers them, and a touch device has no Tab key.

findings.title: Submitting a role-change request notifies the requester on no channel — no email, no in-app notification — despite a stated 24-48 hour review window
findings.summary: Submitting a role-change request notifies the requester on no channel — no email, no in-app notification — despite a stated 24-48 hour review window. Approval does send an email, so the gap is specific to submission.

findings.title: Download Data produces a profile snapshot, not a complete portable personal-data export
findings.summary: Download Data produces a profile snapshot, not a complete portable personal-data export. Data visibly held by CIC—policy acceptance history and preferences—and major account domains are absent.

findings.title: A sensitive personal-data export downloads immediately from an authenticated session without password, MFA or other step-up authentication
findings.summary: A sensitive personal-data export downloads immediately from an authenticated session without password, MFA or other step-up authentication.

findings.title: Account deactivation Submit becomes enabled with only a reason and static phrase
findings.summary: Account deactivation Submit becomes enabled with only a reason and static phrase. There is no password/reconfirmation control, so a session thief can initiate closure and the scenario's wrong-password requirement is impossible.

findings.title: Sell action is inert for valid partial and full listings
findings.summary: The Sell action is inert for valid partial and full listings. Repeated pointer and keyboard submissions produce no progress, success or error, the modal stays open, and the listing count remains zero after refresh.

findings.title: same owned project's displayed current price changed from $57,900.33 to $0 after refresh and remained $0 after ten seconds, while ownership and por…
findings.summary: The same owned project's displayed current price changed from $57,900.33 to $0 after refresh and remained $0 after ten seconds, while ownership and portfolio value did not change and no listing/trade was visible.

findings.title: Both logged-in Change Password and forgot-password recovery accept a canonical common password that the scenario explicitly requires to be rejected
findings.summary: Both logged-in Change Password and forgot-password recovery accept a canonical common password that the scenario explicitly requires to be rejected. The value became a functioning login credential in both paths.

findings.title: Forgot-password recovery accepts the account's existing password and reports a successful change, while logged-in Change Password rejects reuse
findings.summary: Forgot-password recovery accepts the account's existing password and reports a successful change, while logged-in Change Password rejects reuse. This defeats password-history/current-password protection and emits a misleading security event.

findings.title: An explicitly incomplete Assessor can bypass mandatory profile readiness through Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Browse Pitches, open the live as…
findings.summary: An explicitly incomplete Assessor can bypass mandatory profile readiness through Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Browse Pitches, open the live assessment editor, save a completely blank draft, and see the server-persisted Draft row afterward. The control is therefore missing at both navigation and mutation boundaries.

findings.title: Draft assessment is counted as completed
findings.summary: The only authoritative assessment row is Draft, but the Dashboard reports Completed 1, Active Assessments 0, and separately presents the same pitch as pending. This is a direct count/status integrity failure and reproduces at C-360, C-390, C-768, C-1024, C-1280, and C-1440. Impact: assessors and operators cannot trust the dashboard to distinguish unfinished work from completed work. Any completion-based downstream reporting or decisions derived from this card are unsafe.

findings.title: Dashboard amount visibility does not survive navigation
findings.summary: The explicit Show amounts choice revealed both zero balances and remained after a browser refresh, but after opening Wallet and returning through the visible Overview tab the dashboard reverted to hidden. The safe default is preserved, so this is not a disclosure; it is a preference-persistence failure against the scenario requirement.

findings.title: Public-profile entry points do not open the public profile for the current Assessor
findings.summary: Both entry points visibly accept input, but the resulting destination is the private role-completion workspace rather than a public profile. This prevents self-preview and blocks the scenario's authenticated-other-role and guest privacy checks. The actor is genuinely missing an expertise area/specialization; ASS-007 will add those through the UI and this finding must then be retested. If the links are intentionally gated, the UI must explain that before presenting them as public-profile actions.

findings.title: Invalid experience years persist server-side
findings.summary: The specialization accepted and retained -1 years and 999 years after Save Changes and full refresh. The dashboard summary also treated realistic positive values as aggregate experience, while the invalid negative value rendered directly in the card. The API boundary is therefore not enforcing a credible non-negative upper-bounded range. Impact: requester discovery and qualification decisions can be driven by impossible assessor experience claims.

findings.title: Expertise catalogue selection can create a mismatched area
findings.summary: Choosing the visible Technology menu item produced an area headed Tax with Technology's software/platform description. The actor removed the corrupt row and recreated Technology through the custom-entry field. Impact: assessors can publish a category different from the one selected, corrupting search/discovery and profile interpretation.

findings.title: Qualification duplicates are not normalized
findings.summary: With CFA already present, a second qualification entered as spaced/lowercase cfa saved and survived refresh. Credentials increased from 1 to 2 and the summary displayed CFA · +1 more. The duplicate was replaced before handoff.

findings.title: Impossible accomplishment year persists
findings.summary: The accomplishment form accepted 9999; Save Changes succeeded and refresh reproduced the value. The field provides no credible calendar boundary at either client or server persistence layers.

findings.title: Employment date picker displays one year and saves another
findings.summary: The End Date year input visibly showed 2025, but selecting December produced Dec, 2026. The accessibility snapshot likewise continued naming the month choices as 2026 while the rendered picker header showed 2025. Impact: an assessor can unknowingly publish inaccurate employment dates even after visually selecting the intended year.

findings.title: Unsafe javascript: public URL saves and survives refresh
findings.summary: The Website URL field accepted javascript:alert(1), returned the normal success toast, and displayed the exact value after a full refresh and accordion reopen. The payload was not executed. A benign HTTPS URL was restored. Impact: every renderer or outbound-link surface must now defensively reject or neutralize this stored value. Server-side allowlisting to https: (and any explicitly supported safe schemes) is required before go-live.

findings.title: Alias is ignored on the public profile
findings.summary: Bio data labels Alias as “How users see you on the platform” and the saved value persisted as Adebayo-UAT Ω. Every public-profile viewport instead exposes Adebayo Guerrilla-UAT. This defeats the intended public-identity/privacy control and reproduces across all six Chrome sizes.

findings.title: Assessment rate has no credible upper bound
findings.summary: 999999999999999 produced the normal success confirmation and reloaded as 999,999,999,999,999. This value can therefore enter requester-facing pricing and any downstream financial calculation. Enforce a documented, currency-aware maximum on both client and server.

findings.title: Availability and capacity policy cannot be configured
findings.summary: The full Account surface exposes only Free/Paid, USD/NGN and rate. There is no availability state, capacity limit, date range, blackout, timezone, conflict, or pause control, and no alternate requestability policy is explained. The earlier #2209 gap remains open, so unavailable or capacity-full behavior cannot be configured or proven.

findings.title: KYC has no durable partial-save/resume path
findings.summary: Street and postcode remained in the live form across a browser refresh, but Cancel followed by a fresh entry cleared them. There is no Save draft control, saved-progress confirmation, or resume point. A user gathering sensitive evidence across sessions can therefore lose work before the mandatory upload gate.

findings.title: Organization context renders personal security notifications
findings.summary: After switching A1 into CIC Assessor UAT Ω 2026, the Notifications workspace displayed A1's personal password-reset and password-change history. The active actor was the organization and the scenario explicitly requires notification ownership to follow that actor. This mixes personal security events into a shared institutional context and creates a confidentiality risk for organization members.

findings.title: Fresh signup resumes a previous tester's identity draft
findings.summary: Opening the signup flow for a new isolated email on the same collaborative browser reached a confirmation page populated with another tester's name, email and phone (UATClosure Assessor, an uberip.com address and a different phone). The values were visible before correction. This is persistent registration-data remanence across test identities on a shared browser and can expose one applicant's PII to the next person using the device.

findings.title: Keyboard expertise selection displays the filter without applying it
findings.summary: Mouse-selecting Accounting produced no eligible rows. After clearing, typing the same value into the same control and choosing it with ArrowDown/Enter produced the same input text and matching-filter banner but left Uat assessor visible. The directory therefore presents two materially different eligibility result sets for an identical visible filter state. This breaks keyboard access and makes search results untrustworthy.

findings.title: Directory omits required readiness, capacity and profile evidence
findings.summary: The only result exposed a generic name, zero rating, country, an unlabeled type icon, Not provided specialization, Free, and Request. It had no public-profile link, availability/capacity state, KYC/readiness indication, expertise evidence summary, industry match, or reason for eligibility. The required free/paid and converted-currency comparison is also absent. Requesters cannot make or audit the decision this scenario requires.

findings.title: Request handoff loses the selected Assessor identity
findings.summary: After Request was clicked on Uat assessor, the assessment form did not display the Assessor's name, alias, profile, specialization, readiness or directory rate. A requester cannot verify that the scope is being sent to the intended person, violating the scenario's exact-identity handoff requirement and increasing misrouting risk.

findings.title: Minimum Accepted Bids accepts a negative filter value
findings.summary: The advanced numeric filter retained -1 with no validation message or normalization and returned the unfiltered six-pitch set. A minimum-count constraint cannot be negative; accepting it creates an invalid visible query state and unreliable filter semantics.

findings.title: Unverified/KYC-incomplete Assessor is offered volunteer review despite an existing pitch relationship
findings.summary: A1 displayed both the Unverified badge and Complete your KYC requirements, while the dashboard already showed a separate Requestor pending assessment for UAT Solar Microgrid 73110. The same pitch nevertheless exposed enabled Write Free Review. The scenario explicitly requires incomplete-profile/KYC, already-hired and conflict variants to be blocked before draft creation or recovery.

findings.title: Existing volunteer draft is hidden until Write Free Review is clicked
findings.summary: Before the action, the Assessment table was empty and the UI offered Write Free Review. Clicking it immediately replaced that state with a Draft/You row. Opening the row showed the same review ID had last been saved at 02:34:17, well before this run. Existing work must be surfaced as Resume/Edit on initial load; presenting a creation action for hidden state makes duplicate/conflict behavior impossible to reason about.

findings.title: Dashboard omits the volunteer draft shown in Manage Assessments
findings.summary: Manage Assessments displayed the pitch as a free Draft and the pitch Assessment row persisted it after refresh. The dashboard still reported Active Assessments 0 and surfaced only a different Requestor pending card for that pitch. This fails the scenario's traceable-draft requirement and gives the Assessor conflicting work queues.

findings.title: Ambiguous retry creates a duplicate paid request instead of reconciling one intent
findings.summary: After the first request was known successful, P1 deliberately reopened the identical form to exercise retry protection. The first click in that retry attempt disabled the Request button; a rapid second click could not target the disabled control. The app then reported it could not confirm the session, making the retry outcome ambiguous. After login/reload, two identical paid rows existed in P1 Hires, A1 dashboard, A1 Requests and A1 Notifications. The server must reject/reconcile equivalent in-flight or recent retries with an idempotency boundary and return an unambiguous outcome. A duplicate second wallet hold is plausible but was not counted as proven because the wallet view could not be recovered before role change.

findings.title: Request CTAs lose object identity and open unrelated default work
findings.summary: Both the in-app Open notification action and the actual email's View the request link navigated to /manage-assessments with no request identifier. The workspace defaulted to the Assessments tab and unrelated volunteer work; the Assessor had to discover the Requests tab and infer which indistinguishable row was intended. This also prevented request-specific wrong-account, expiry, deleted/private pitch and missing-object authorization checks.

findings.title: Real email shifts response deadlines one calendar day earlier
findings.summary: The paid request displayed 15 September 2026 in both requester and Assessor UI, but its email stated 14 September. The free request displayed 16 September in the UI, but its inbox preview stated 15 September. Reproducing the same -1 day error on consecutive dates is consistent with an incorrect timezone/date-only conversion and can cause premature expiry or missed contractual response windows.

findings.title: Free request email is described as a paid-assessment request
findings.summary: The free variant was published and submitted at NGN 0.00, and the in-app notification correctly displayed that amount. Its real-email subject/preview nevertheless said You have a new paid-assessment request. The message misstates the commercial nature of the request even while presenting a zero fee.

findings.title: Durable request, notification and email counts diverge
findings.summary: A1 retained three request rows/cards and three corresponding in-app notifications: two paid duplicates and one free request. The actual mailbox contained only two emails, one for the paid requester/pitch and one for the free requester/pitch. Exactly-once delivery is broken in opposite directions across channels, leaving no reliable audit trail for which committed financial request was communicated.

findings.title: Investor requester's Hires view does not reconcile its successful request
findings.summary: I1 submitted the free request successfully and A1 immediately received the resulting card and notification. Returning to the same pitch's Hires tab as I1 produced no row after tab toggling and reload. The requester therefore cannot confirm or manage the request it created. I1 was also acting on a P1-owned pitch because the application exposed Hire Assessor to the non-owner Investor, repeating G-A16 from ASS-011.

findings.title: Decision dialog omits essential request identity and commercial context
findings.summary: The Requests table contained requester, status, response deadline, due date and fee, but Accept/Reject reduced the decision to pitch title, delivery date, fee and tasks. It omitted requester identity, assessment type, response deadline, current status and explicit currency code. A1 therefore cannot verify the complete request inside the very surface where irreversible acceptance/rejection occurs. The free Review comparator had the same omissions.

findings.title: Scope and request-document workflows are absent
findings.summary: The non-Review request builder exposed only 1–3 task text fields; there was no scope, requester note, attachment, public/private classification, or permitted pitch-document selector. The A1 decision surface offered no scope, attachment list, pitch/deck link, preview or download action. Consequently no public/private/removed-file authorization, safe filename/content-type, or least-privilege document decision can be made through the product.

findings.title: Legal documents cannot support versioned, auditable consent
findings.summary: Both documents were readable, but neither displayed a version, publication/effective date, governing-policy identifier or supersession marker. A checkbox submission can therefore record only a generic boolean from the visible workflow, not which terms were presented and accepted. This prevents a reliable legal audit trail when content changes.

findings.title: Duplicate tasks are accepted without detection or clarification
findings.summary: P1 entered the exact same 92-character task twice. The request submitted successfully, Edit preserved both values, and A1 was required to check two visually identical obligations. The builder should either prevent exact duplicates or require the requester to disambiguate them so completion evidence maps to a unique obligation.

findings.title: Zero-task validation remains after the form is corrected
findings.summary: After the empty submission, the form displayed an actionable zero-task error. Adding three non-empty tasks did not clear that error; it remained visible next to 92/250, 92/250 and 250/250 counters until the successful submission removed the dialog. Stale error state makes a corrected request appear invalid and undermines recovery feedback.

findings.title: Accepted requests are stranded outside the Assessor workspaces
findings.summary: Both Requests rows became Accepted, but A1's dashboard continued to show Active Assessments 0. Manage Assessments → Assessments showed only an unrelated historical volunteer draft, Assigned Projects showed zero items, and the accepted dashboard card routed back to generic Requests without a response action. The request-specific response form exists and works when A1 is manually given the requester-side URL, so this is a discovery/assignment-integration failure that prevents normal delivery.

findings.title: Requesters can open the Assessor's editable submission form
findings.summary: While visibly authenticated as P1, the real paid acceptance email CTA and the matching in-app notification opened the Technology Assessment Response form with all requested tasks, comment fields, attachment upload and Submit Assessment. Independently, I1's free acceptance notification opened the editable Review Assessment Response form. A requester must never receive authorization to author or upload the Assessor's deliverable. Server-side submission authorization was not destructively probed in ASS-015 and must be covered by the dedicated authorization retest.

findings.title: Free acceptance communications claim a zero-value wallet hold
findings.summary: I1's in-app notification and real email say NGN 0.00 has been reserved from your wallet; the email then says that this fee is held until the assessment is completed. The free request created no wallet transaction, so the communication invents a financial operation and can confuse the requester. Free acceptance content should explicitly state that no charge or reservation was made.

findings.title: Rejection is an unconfirmed one-click action with no required reason
findings.summary: The Reject dialog accepted an empty Notes field and its Reject button immediately committed the terminal state. There was no explicit confirmation/review step, no opportunity to cancel after the destructive click, and no reason was shown in the requester notification/email or retained in the visible terminal record. Accidental or unexplained rejection therefore cannot be distinguished or audited.

findings.title: One rejection is represented as two positive wallet reversals and rewrites the original hold
findings.summary: P1's available balance correctly increased once by NGN 25,000, but wallet history added a new positive Refund row while changing the original negative assessment hold into another positive declined/Cancelled reservation-release row that retained the old hold reference. A financial audit cannot reconstruct the original reservation and sees two apparent credits for one balance movement. Reservation and reversal must be immutable, separately referenced entries whose signed amounts reconcile exactly to the displayed balance.

findings.title: Requester cancellation removes the record but leaves NGN 25,000 locked
findings.summary: The unlabeled Hires action committed cancellation in one click without confirmation or reason. The request disappeared from both role workspaces instead of persisting as Cancelled, no notification/email was delivered, and P1's available balance did not recover: the NGN 25,000 hold remained in the wallet. This both strands requester funds and eliminates the user-visible audit trail.

findings.title: Response-deadline expiry is not enforced and expired requests can be accepted
findings.summary: After their stored response deadlines passed, requests remained Pending and actionable, with holds still locked and no Expired state or communication. Acceptance succeeded from both a dialog opened before the boundary and an independent dialog opened only after expiry; each persisted Accepted after reload and generated an acceptance email. The UI exposes only a calendar date without a time, timezone or countdown, but the fresh-dialog result establishes a server-backed lifecycle failure rather than merely ambiguous display copy.

findings.title: Incoming paid-request emails were not delivered to the Assessor
findings.summary: A1 received both requests in-app, but the actual Guerrilla Mail inbox never received either A16E1 or A16E2 incoming-request email. Earlier request emails remained visible, demonstrating mailbox continuity. Missing delivery removes the required off-platform prompt for time-sensitive response deadlines.

findings.title: Negative rates are silently converted into positive proposals
findings.summary: Typing -100 removed the minus sign, displayed 100 and enabled Send Proposal. A destructive financial input must be rejected with clear inline feedback, not transformed into a materially different valid offer.

findings.title: Proposal input has no defensible upper bound or affordability guard
findings.summary: A 20-digit NGN amount was formatted normally and left Send Proposal enabled with no maximum, warning or confirmation. This creates fat-finger and abuse exposure far beyond the requester's wallet and ordinary assessment values.

findings.title: Negotiation notes are double-escaped across application and email
findings.summary: The submitted < character rendered as the literal text < for A1, P1 and the real email. Notes otherwise persisted, so this is a consistent presentation/encoding defect rather than input loss.

findings.title: Proposal success can be reported without durable persistence
findings.summary: Two A17E NGN 40,000 submissions displayed a success toast while the request stayed Pending at NGN 25,000 after refresh. A later clean-session NGN 42,000 retry persisted. Success must not be announced until the durable state is confirmed, and idempotent recovery must make the final outcome unambiguous.

findings.title: Assessor-authored rates are mislabeled as client proposals
findings.summary: After A17A acceptance and A17R rejection, A1's own Requests cards labeled the value Client proposed rate. The requester did not author either proposal. This reverses negotiation authorship in the audit presentation.

findings.title: Assessor does not receive rate-outcome notifications or complete email delivery
findings.summary: A1 received the requests in-app, but no acceptance/rejection outcome appeared after P1 responded. Its real mailbox received neither the three A17 incoming-request emails nor any rate outcome email, while P1's proposal notifications/emails arrived. Time-sensitive negotiation cannot rely on one-sided delivery.

findings.title: Request copy misstates when funds are committed
findings.summary: The requester modal says funds are committed only after the final negotiated rate is accepted, yet submitting each base-rate request immediately created an NGN 25,000 reservation hold. The financial copy must accurately explain the initial reservation and later delta adjustment.

findings.title: Date-only assessment terms shift one day earlier in actual emails
findings.summary: The live UI showed A18E's proposed due date as 6 October 2026, while P1's delivered counter-offer email showed 5 October. The same email retained the Assessor's prose saying 6 October, making it internally contradictory. Separately, A18A's response deadline displayed as 20 September in the app but 19 September in A1's request email. Date-only commercial deadlines must use one documented timezone/calendar representation in every channel.

findings.title: Request search omits visible Unicode, rate and assessment-type data
findings.summary: The queue contained Ω in every pitch title, yet searching Ω returned no matches. Searching the visible NGN value 25,000 also returned none. Searching Review returned only two A17 rows even though known Review records exceed that result. Exact title, requester and status searches passed, demonstrating that the control works but indexes an inconsistent subset of the work-item model.

findings.title: Search is neither debounced nor programmatically named
findings.summary: Typing leaves the previous result set unchanged until Enter is pressed, contrary to the scenario's debounced-loading requirement. The visible Search placeholder does not provide an accessible name: the live input was exposed with an empty name. Add an explicit label/accessible name, defined submit behavior if intended, loading announcement, and consistent keyboard/pointer behavior.

findings.title: Request workspace drops due-date negotiation rationale
findings.summary: A18E was accepted after a due-date-only proposal with a submitted reason, but the request queue labelled its note control No negotiation note. A18A contained separate due-date and rate reasons, yet the queue dialog showed only the rate text. Assessors cannot reconstruct why the operative due date changed from this primary work queue.

findings.title: Assignment sub-navigation changes URL/highlight but keeps the assessment form
findings.summary: From a valid saved-draft route, selecting Overview, Pitch Deck or Information Request updates the sidebar highlight and changes tab=1, tab=5 or tab=6. The page body nevertheless remains the editable Assessment rubric. The Assessor cannot obtain the required source context, evidence or Q&A from this contracted-work shell, and route state no longer describes rendered content.

findings.title: Assessment search is case- and whitespace-sensitive
findings.summary: The exact identifier P7SUN returned the saved row, but p7sun and p7sun both produced the no-match state. This differs from the Requests workspace, where lowercase and padded title variants passed in ASS-019. Normalize case and surrounding whitespace consistently before searching.

findings.title: Organization context can directly load the personal actor's editable draft
findings.summary: After switching to the organization actor, its assessment list correctly showed zero records. The personal P7SUN draft nevertheless stayed fully editable in the already-open route, and refreshing the same reviewId URL in organization context loaded the full editable rubric again. Context-aware authorization/list visibility disagree, creating an attribution and cross-context data-integrity risk.

findings.title: Logout discards the active assignment return route
findings.summary: Logging out from the saved draft navigated to bare /login. Logging back in as A1 reached /dashboard, not the assessment. Direct guest access does provide a protected-pitch interstitial whose Log in link carries the complete returnUrl, so the continuity capability exists but is not used by explicit logout.

findings.title: Non-Review assessment answers cannot be saved and are lost on refresh
findings.summary: The Technology response page offers only Submit Assessment. It has no Save draft, autosave state, unsaved-change warning or recovery path. After valid independent answers made Submit ready, refreshing the exact assignment route reset every task comment and the overall assessment to zero. A multi-task professional assessment cannot safely be completed over more than one sitting.

findings.title: Structured tasks collapse to untyped comments without contract context
findings.summary: The accepted assignment exposes only prompt text and a minimum-50-character textarea per task. It omits required/optional status, answer type, helper text, response/due deadlines, accepted rate/currency, requester, aggregate progress and dependency behavior. The upstream request UI also provided no way to author numeric, choice, boolean, date, URL or conditional tasks. The planned structured-task contract therefore cannot be represented end to end.

findings.title: Review validation is bottom-only and does not focus invalid fields
findings.summary: Both empty and partial Submit actions leave the viewport at the top with no inline guidance. A combined error appears only below the entire 16-row rubric, and it reports All assessment scores rather than identifying individual categories. Keyboard and screen-reader users receive no focus movement to the first problem.

findings.title: Recommendation options are bidding tactics rather than assessment conclusions
findings.summary: The required Recommendation field offers equity bargaining and timing tactics, including delaying a bid until the last minute for bargaining power. The values do not define a neutral conclusion such as recommend, recommend with conditions, request more evidence or do not recommend, so a professional assessment cannot record a clear independent outcome.

findings.title: The 1–5 rubric has no scale definitions
findings.summary: Sixteen unrelated categories use the same stars, but the page provides no label for what 1 versus 5 means, whether a higher score is always better, or evidence thresholds. Assessors cannot apply the rubric consistently and requesters cannot interpret the aggregate reliably.

findings.title: Completed Review submits irreversibly without confirmation
findings.summary: Activating Submit on a fully populated review immediately persisted it and displayed success. There is no confirmation dialog, final read-only summary, acknowledgement of requester visibility, or cancel window despite the absence of any later edit action in the canonical submitted viewer.

findings.title: Submitted review's original draft URL still exposes Save and Submit
findings.summary: The canonical submitted viewer is read-only, but navigating back to the exact reviewId URL used before submission renders an empty editable rubric with Save as draft and Submit. This breaks terminal-state enforcement at the UI boundary and exposes duplicate/overwrite risk. The actual second-submit outcome is carried into ASS-025.

findings.title: Submitted assessment has a blank Status cell
findings.summary: After the volunteer review persisted and the dashboard labelled it completed, the Manage Assessments row showed title, three-star rounded rating, date and Free charge but no Status value. Users cannot distinguish draft, submitted or other terminal states from the authoritative work list.

findings.title: Empty and unchanged draft saves have no dirty-state guard
findings.summary: Save as draft accepts a completely empty Review and remains enabled immediately after acknowledgement. Activating it again with no changes performs another save and updates the saved state without explaining whether a version was created. The UI provides no dirty, saving, unchanged or version indicator to prevent redundant writes or communicate what changed.

findings.title: Assessments-list resume opens an incompatible form and strands rubric data
findings.summary: The authoritative saved-work row is correctly labelled Draft, but activating its title opens Review Assessment Response, a generic single 0/5000-character answer. It contains none of the saved 16 category ratings/comments, four selects or Notes. The request queue's Continue assessment route still restores the rubric, so the data exists but the documented list/dashboard resume path sends the Assessor to the wrong editor.

findings.title: Stale tab silently overwrites newer draft fields
findings.summary: Two tabs loaded the same saved baseline. Tab B saved a newer row 1 rating/comment and Notes. Tab A, without reloading, changed only row 8 and saved later. No conflict/version warning appeared. Reloading proved tab B's independent newer values were replaced by tab A's stale baseline while tab A's row 8 edit won. The draft service therefore applies last-write-wins to the whole record and silently loses acknowledged professional work.

findings.title: Navigation discards unsaved draft edits without warning
findings.summary: After changing Notes, activating the account Overview tab immediately navigated to Dashboard. There was no confirmation, before-leave prompt, autosave or recovery notice. Reopening the assignment restored only the previous saved Note, proving the unsaved edit was discarded.

findings.title: Exact duplicate RFIs are accepted as independent requests
findings.summary: After one RFI was durably visible, A1 reopened the composer and submitted the exact same title, description and due date. The table immediately contained two indistinguishable Open rows. There was no warning, merge behavior or idempotency protection, so a retry can create duplicate obligations and conflicting closure histories.

findings.title: RFI creation and response produce no in-app notification or email
findings.summary: P1's notification badge remained 15 and its real YOPmail inbox remained 18 after two RFI creations. After P1 answered, A1's badge remained at its pre-run baseline of 24, the newest notification page contained only older assessment-request events, and its real Guerrilla Mail inbox contained no RFI response. Neither actor receives a CTA/deep link for time-sensitive Q&A.

findings.title: Whitespace response can close an RFI with blank persisted content
findings.summary: The owner composer displayed Response Message Cannot be empty for whitespace. Without any later valid submission on that first row, it then became Closed/On Time. Opening the detail as both P1 and A1 showed an empty Response. The system therefore commits a state the client says is invalid, irreversibly closes the request and loses the required answer.

findings.title: RFI is a one-shot close, not an auditable Q&A lifecycle
findings.summary: Open detail omits assignment/request identity, requester, status, due date and timestamps. Sending the first response automatically closes the record; closed detail provides no responder identity, response timestamp, attachment history, acknowledgement, explicit close, correction, follow-up or reopen control. The requester and Assessor cannot manage clarification or establish who did what when.

findings.title: Later valid RFI submissions silently disappear
findings.summary: After both initial RFIs were closed, A1 twice entered a new title, valid description and future due date. Each Request action dismissed the composer, but no success or error appeared and the count stayed at two after waiting and refresh. If a maximum exists it is undisclosed; otherwise valid work is silently lost.

findings.title: Final Review accepts an assessment with almost every category comment blank
findings.summary: The form says Please fill out all fields, yet the paid Review became terminal with valid scores and only two of 16 category comments. Both Assessor and requester canonical viewers show 14 em dashes. A supposedly complete professional deliverable can therefore omit nearly all written justification, and the contract presented to the user contradicts the enforced contract.

findings.title: Completed paid Review remains reserved with no observed settlement path
findings.summary: A18A changed to Completed and exposed its final 1.56 output, but P1's NGN 25,000 and NGN 13,000 entries remained Reservation Holds, P1 available balance remained NGN 210,000, and A1 available balance remained zero. Unlike Technology, the Review output exposed no Pay Now/Need More Time/Dispute panel. The NGN 38,000 engagement is terminal in work state but not financially finalizable from the reached UI.

findings.title: Final assessment completion is not delivered in app or by email
findings.summary: Neither A18A Review nor A14T1 Technology generated a completion notification for the requester or Assessor, and neither real test mailbox received a completion message. A1 received an in-app event only after P1 manually paid Technology; no payment email reached either mailbox. Users cannot reliably discover a deliverable or retain off-platform delivery proof.

findings.title: Technology Task 2 persists Task 1's answer
findings.summary: Task 1 and Task 2 intentionally used the same prompt but received distinct answers and distinct pre-submit counters (118 and 119 characters). The terminal response shown to both P1 and A1 repeats Task 1's 118-character answer under Task 2. Task 2's submitted answer is lost, corrupting the signed-off professional output.

findings.title: Successful Technology capture removes value from the Assessor balance
findings.summary: P1's NGN 25,000 payment correctly reduced requester current balance from NGN 500,000 to NGN 475,000 and changed the reservation to Capture/Success. A1's corresponding +NGN 25,000 ledger row also says Reservation Capture/Success and produced a paid notification, but A1 current balance fell from NGN 290,000 to NGN 265,000 while available balance stayed NGN 0. The UI therefore reports a successful payer debit and recipient credit event while making the recipient NGN 25,000 worse off and providing no spendable earnings.

findings.title: No explicit post-submission rework lifecycle exists
findings.summary: Requester P1 can read both terminal types and see Completed Hires, but there is no Request revision/Rework action, reason dialog, pending state, cancel, duplicate prevention, accept/reject decision or assessor work item. Technology chat becomes read-only after payout; Review exposes only ordinary chat. A correction therefore cannot be initiated through a permissioned, auditable workflow, so every reason, notification, rework-edit, resubmission and resolution branch in this scenario is unreachable.

findings.title: Terminal assessments have no version identity or revision audit surface
findings.summary: The canonical Review and Technology views show content and author, but no version number, immutable original identifier, submitted/finalized timestamps, change history, requested-change scope, comparison or attachment lineage. Even if support manually changed data, users could not distinguish the signed original from a correction or audit who finalized which version.

findings.title: UI declares an overdue hold released while the wallet remains reserved
findings.summary: A18E was more than 80 hours past its due time. Both roles rendered Deadline Missed and Auto-failed; hold released, and the Assessor could no longer save. Nevertheless, P1's NGN 25,000 reservation remained pending and available balance did not increase after the lifecycle window. A financial terminal state must not be announced before its settlement commits, and the scheduler must idempotently release the hold.

findings.title: Pending requester holds contaminate the Assessor current balance
findings.summary: A1 current balance fell NGN 265,000→240,000 when an unpaid held request was terminated, then returned to NGN 265,000 when P1 created a new NGN 25,000 held request. A1 available balance remained zero throughout. The Assessor's current balance therefore includes money that has neither been paid nor made available, and termination appears to debit the Assessor. Pending escrow must be represented separately from owned/current funds.

findings.title: One termination release is represented twice and its receipt reverses the money direction
findings.summary: P1 correctly regained NGN 25,000 available once, but the history shows both a new positive Refund row and the original reservation mutated into a positive Reservation Release row. The new refund receipt then labels P1 as Sender and Assessor as Recipient even though the funds returned to P1. The ledger must retain an immutable negative hold plus one clearly linked release/refund, with correct sender/recipient semantics.

findings.title: Requester cancellation/termination is unavailable outside the late window
findings.summary: Before lateness, an accepted Hires row exposed only chat. After submission, the Technology record exposed payment, extension and dispute controls but no cancellation/termination action. Terminate appeared only after the seeded late state. The product therefore cannot execute or audit the required pre-start, in-progress and post-submission cancellation branches.

findings.title: Deadline, auto-fail and termination events send no in-app or email communication
findings.summary: Neither A18E's auto-fail claim nor A18R's committed termination produced an A1 notification or real email. No reminder or exact boundary message was observed. Adverse financial lifecycle changes need role-appropriate in-app and email delivery with a valid, authorized link.

findings.title: Dispute alert has no usable Assessor response or record deep link
findings.summary: A1 received a correct notification and real email, but both links landed on generic /manage-assessments. The NGN 25,000 assessment row had a blank Status. Opening the exact submission showed no Filed badge, dispute type, reason, timestamp, evidence or Respond/Acknowledge action; only the ordinary chat became read-only. The email explicitly instructs the Assessor to respond through the platform, which is impossible. P1 also received no filing confirmation in app or email, and no administration decision/audit surface was exposed.

findings.title: Eligible requesters cannot rate completed Assessor work
findings.summary: P1 owns completed paid Review and Technology engagements with A1, including one fully paid Technology output. Neither canonical output, Hires row, profile nor Feedback center exposes a requester-to-Assessor score/comment action. There is no prior rating indicator or edit policy. Every required authorization, numeric-boundary, long/unsafe comment, cancel, duplicate and stale-tab rating check is therefore impossible, and A1 cannot accrue reputation from delivered work.

findings.title: Assessor reputation has no auditable aggregate or rating history
findings.summary: The request directory renders A1 as (0), every Manage Assessments My Rating cell is blank, and the authenticated public profile renders badges/score but no rating average, count, comments, engagement link or rating history. Users cannot distinguish unrated from zero-rated, reconcile directory/profile/list state, or verify arithmetic. Badge score 25 is a different metric and is not labelled as an assessment rating.

findings.title: Report workflows are inconsistent and provide no durable reporter audit trail
findings.summary: The Q&A Report action commits immediately with no reason, target summary, confirmation or cancel and becomes only Already reported. Report profile has a reason and optional details plus Cancel, but after submit the profile simply returns with Report profile still enabled. Neither report appears in the Feedback status center or creates a reporter notification/email. Target non-notification can protect reporter privacy, but the submitting user cannot retain a receipt, reference or moderation status.

findings.title: Reciprocal settled receipts disagree on payer/payee direction
findings.summary: P1's receipt for the NGN 25,000 A14T1 capture identifies Ngozi as Sender and Assessor as Recipient. A1's corresponding receipt identifies Adebayo as Sender, Requestor as Recipient and Requestor as Provider. Both say settled transfer and net recipient NGN 25,000, but cannot both describe the same money direction. This makes the audit document unreliable even before comparing the broken balances.

findings.title: Linked financial-account UI is not credibly user-scoped or usable for payout
findings.summary: Two isolated users display the exact same USD/NGN/GBP bank aliases, masked account suffix 0123 and four Spending Card suffixes/06/23 expiry dates. A1's withdrawal payout selector nevertheless says No options. The account page therefore exposes fixture-like financial data as if linked to each personal profile while not producing a selectable payout account.

findings.title: Approved-KYC Assessor cannot configure or complete any withdrawal
findings.summary: A1 is visibly KYC Valid, but NGN withdrawal says NGN bank payouts available and NGN payout setup unavailable in the same dialog. Add payout account only redirects back to this dead end. With no selectable account, valid/minimum/maximum withdrawal, confirmation, idempotency and every pending/success/failure/reversal state are unreachable.

findings.title: Wallet sort controls are inert
findings.summary: Date and Amount are exposed as clickable table-header controls. Starting from the same ten-row A1 page, two Date clicks and one Amount click left the row order unchanged and exposed no ascending/descending indicator. Search, filters and pagination work, so this is isolated to sorting.

findings.title: Active Assessor project is absent from Assigned Projects
findings.summary: A1 has a working temporary-access route, appears in the owner's roster and can see its accepted hire. Assigned Projects nevertheless reports zero rows. An exact-title search returns no match, leaving the Assessor dependent on a guessed or externally supplied URL.

findings.title: Temporary Assessor can read exact project-wallet balances
findings.summary: The temporary-access project exposes NGN 100,000 available, NGN 25,000 pending/held and NGN 125,000 current. The scenario requires the wallet and bank/account controls to remain hidden or denied; this is direct financial-data disclosure outside the assignment's assessment scope.

findings.title: Completed/ended engagement retains private read/write project access
findings.summary: A1's completed A14T1 engagement still opens the project and private ended-phase milestone without a temporary-access banner. The Assessor successfully changed the milestone from zero to one Support vote, and the mutation survived a full refresh. Post-boundary access is therefore neither read-only nor revoked.

findings.title: Organization actor inherits a personal assignment's milestone access
findings.summary: After switching from A1 Personal into an organization with zero assigned projects, a direct A16E1 milestone URL still rendered the personal assignment's private milestone and write controls. The temporary-access banner disappeared, so the application both loses the contracted actor identity and keeps the underlying personal authorization.

findings.title: Project RFI has no owner response or communications lifecycle
findings.summary: A1 can create an RFI and P1 can read it, but the owner detail has no answer/response action. No new owner notification was present and the real test inbox remained unchanged after refresh. The persisted open RFI is therefore operationally stranded.

findings.title: Milestone comment submission silently loses valid content
findings.summary: The comment modal accepted long Unicode and harmless HTML-like text. Post comment closed the modal, but immediate and refreshed milestone views remained at zero comments/discussions and no error explained the loss.

findings.title: Project owner cannot revoke displayed temporary access
findings.summary: The owner roster explains the temporary grant and expiry, while Hires shows the accepted engagement. Neither exposes revoke, end access, cancel or equivalent control, so immediate removal cannot be performed through the authorized owner UI.

findings.title: Schedule commits while the browser reports insufficient credit
findings.summary: Submitting the P1 schedule form left the modal open with Insufficient session credit, yet the exact session already existed in the browser list and opened normally. A host can retry a committed action because the UI represents success as failure.

findings.title: Session communications corrupt timezone and duration
findings.summary: The product page showed 13:05 local while the schedule communication showed 12:05. Reschedule communications repeated the one-hour offset. A 1,800-second duration was labelled 1800 minutes instead of 30 minutes. These errors can make participants miss the live event.

findings.title: Session invitation and membership authorization are absent
findings.summary: There is no invite/remove control or membership roster. A fresh unrelated Assessor and an unrelated Investor could open future, live and ended session URLs, receive Participant permissions, enter live rooms and read persisted chat/recording metadata. Access is effectively possession of the URL plus any logged-in account.

findings.title: Cancelled session exposes an active join path and live room
findings.summary: After P1 confirmed cancellation, the session page displayed Unavailable but retained Join live room. Uninvited A2 clicked it and entered a room labelled SESSION IN PROGRESS, so cancellation does not close the live authorization boundary.

findings.title: Participant capacity and queue are not enforced
findings.summary: The fixture visibly identified itself as a one-seat capacity prerequisite. A1, A2 and unrelated I1 all entered; the participant panel showed three people and no waiting, queue, admission or rejection state.

findings.title: Host entry auto-starts without required prejoin and device workflow
findings.summary: Opening at the boundary immediately marked the session in progress. There was no explicit Start confirmation, camera/microphone preview, device selector, no-device branch or hand-raise control. Permission failures were either raw Agora errors or silent control resets.

findings.title: Leave and participant presence become mutually inconsistent
findings.summary: Navigating away did not warn or promptly remove A1 from P1's roster. Explicit Leave told A1 the session had ended and exposed processed-recording copy while P1 remained live; P1 retained the stale participant. A1 could rejoin afterward.

findings.title: Chat, reply, report and ended-state controls are unreliable
findings.summary: A1's top-level message reached P1 only after reload. Reply submit cleared without creating a reply, Report gave no feedback, Like changed ordering, and the ended session kept an enabled composer whose submits silently disappeared. Although literal HTML-like text was safely escaped, the collaboration and audit trail are not reliable.

findings.title: Completion summaries misstate participants and end time
findings.summary: The room showed two participants, the host completion communication said one, and the pitch card said zero. The card displayed scheduled end instead of actual host-confirmed end. Usage reconciliation therefore cannot be trusted as a faithful session record.

findings.title: Assessor lifecycle communications are incomplete
findings.summary: A1 received no completion, reschedule or cancellation event/email and has no session history/directory. At the reminder boundary A1 and A2 each got one correct in-app reminder and deep link, but neither real inbox received a reminder by 14:05.

findings.title: Host lifecycle communications have wrong identity/content and broken CTA
findings.summary: Cancellation messaging tells the host they registered interest in their own session, reschedule content omits useful time/duration in app, emails carry the timezone/duration corruption, and the cancellation email CTA opens the application homepage rather than the session.

findings.title: Fresh Assessor transactional email does not arrive
findings.summary: A2 completed browser signup and requested resend/login delivery. The product reported success and created matching in-app verification/login notifications, but the visibly refreshed YOPmail inbox remained empty. P1's inbox on the same provider received session lifecycle mail during this run, so this is not treated as a provider-wide evidence outage.

findings.title: Eligibility filter includes a deliberately ineligible grant
findings.summary: A2 visibly contradicts the seed's Male, Aerospace Manufacturing and Canada/Ontario requirements. Eligible for you still leaves that grant in the catalogue. This makes the filter unsafe for applicant decision-making and agrees with the later server-enforcement failure.

findings.title: Invalid custom URL fails without applicant-facing feedback
findings.summary: Submitting notaurl in the optional URL answer leaves the modal open after a failed request, but no field error, toast or recovery instruction appears. The applicant cannot distinguish validation failure from a frozen submit.

findings.title: Application decision notification has no deep-link action
findings.summary: The rejected applicant receives correct public feedback in-app, but that event exposes no Open notification control. The actual email does provide a working View grant link, making delivery behavior inconsistent across channels.

findings.title: Draft invitation exposes Join and returns a generic server error
findings.summary: An invited Assessor sees the draft private grant and a functioning-looking Join modal. Final Join produces only Internal Server Error. The UI should suppress Join until the grant is joinable or explain the owner action required.

findings.title: Fixed co-grantor invitation falsely states that funds will be deducted
findings.summary: The private invitation required no contribution and A1 had zero available funds. The modal nevertheless stated that NGN 75,000 would be deducted. This is materially misleading financial consent copy even though no contribution was actually recorded.

findings.title: Anonymous co-grantor identity leaks across owner channels
findings.summary: A1 selected Join anonymously. P1's Grantors table, in-app acceptance event and actual acceptance email all identify Adebayo Guerrilla-UAT. The option promises name privacy from grantors/applicants but does not enforce it for the creator-facing downstream state.

findings.title: Grantors tab count is zero while two members are listed
findings.summary: Both A1 and P1 views display Grantors (0) above a table containing the creator and A1. The count cannot be relied on for membership/reconciliation.

findings.title: Closed grant keeps active Apply flow
findings.summary: The guest page visibly says Closed with a past deadline yet keeps Apply and Fund active. Apply routes through Login and opens the full application modal for A2. The server correctly rejects Submit and Save Draft, but users are invited into an impossible workflow.

findings.title: Closed catalogue filter returns open grants
findings.summary: After selecting Closed, the headline changes to Explore closed grants, but the eligible, review and ineligible ASS-032 grants—each visibly open—remain in the result set. Status discovery is not trustworthy.

findings.title: Server accepts an application from an ineligible Assessor
findings.summary: The deliberately ineligible grant lists three criteria contradicted by A2. The UI opens Apply and the server accepts the completed application, which persists as Already Applied. Eligibility is neither communicated accurately nor enforced.

findings.title: Literal HTML-shaped message content is silently discarded
findings.summary: The composer accepted literal <script>…</script>, no code executed, but both tags and the enclosed inert text disappeared from the rendered message. Sanitization is effective against execution but changes user-authored content without warning.

findings.title: Unsent chat draft is lost on refresh
findings.summary: An exact Unicode draft was visible in the composer before refresh. Reopening the same conversation returned an empty composer with no recovery notice.

findings.title: Long unbroken message overflows the conversation viewport
findings.summary: A 1,536-character unbroken token inside a 1,577-character message persisted but extended beyond the message bubble instead of wrapping, hiding content horizontally.

findings.title: Cancelled assessment conversation remains writable
findings.summary: The request workspace labels the Accounting request Cancelled. Its assessment conversation still exposes an enabled composer and accepted ASS-033 post-termination message should be blocked Ω; the message remained after refresh. The failed/deadline-missed variant correctly becomes read-only, proving the lifecycle policy is inconsistent.

findings.title: Completed assessment has no chat entry point
findings.summary: The completed Technology assessment renders in Manage Assessments but its six-column row contains no action or chat control. The required completed-assignment communication path cannot be reached through the UI.

findings.title: System-created assessment context is labelled as the Assessor's message
findings.summary: The automatically generated This conversation was created for the Review assessment... event is rendered with Your message. That misattributes system provenance and weakens the chat's audit semantics.

findings.title: Assessment request chat actions begin outside the desktop viewport
findings.summary: At 1440×900, the Requests table initially ends at the deadline/status columns. Chat/actions sit beyond the right edge and only appear after scrolling the table horizontally, making the primary workflow undiscoverable at a standard desktop width.

findings.title: Global unread badge remains stale after page-level read state reaches zero
findings.summary: After opening individual events and then using Mark page as read, the Notifications page persisted zero unread and rendered the correct empty Unread state. The global account-tab badge still showed five through a full refresh. Only logout/login removed it. This leaves users with contradictory notification state and can cause repeated, fruitless checks for unread work.

findings.title: Enabled feedback launcher is absent, blocking every feedback submission branch
findings.summary: Feedback says the movable launcher is visible on every page and its setting successfully toggles off/on. With the setting on, fully loaded Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Wallet pages expose no launcher or submission control. A user therefore cannot create even a basic feedback report, and the expected status/admin lifecycle has no originating record.

findings.title: Assistant reports irrelevant answers as 95% high-confidence grounded help
findings.summary: The safe navigation prompt explicitly asked how to reach the Assessor dashboard and assigned assessments. The response instead defined roles, wallets and grants, while displaying High confidence, 95% and Grounded answer. Citations are present but do not make the response useful for the requested task.

findings.title: Assistant support handoff reports success without creating an actionable handoff
findings.summary: Contact support shows Support handoff requested, but it neither navigates nor returns a correlation reference. Opening Support immediately afterward shows no active session or handoff-created request. Users can reasonably believe a human escalation exists when none is visible.

findings.title: Assistant omits privacy refusal and irreversible-action safeguards
findings.summary: Requests for another user's private assessment data and for immediate account closure/fund withdrawal both receive unrelated 95% high-confidence generic answers. No private data was disclosed and no write occurred, but the product does not state the privacy boundary, refuse the request or warn that irreversible financial/account actions require confirmation.

findings.title: Assistant silently truncates long prompts before persistence
findings.summary: The 1,534-character prompt was fully visible before send. Its persisted audit retains the start and only 148 of 180 repeated tokens; the explicit end marker is absent. There is no visible maximum, counter, validation or truncation warning, yet the Assistant answers the incomplete value.

findings.title: Unrelated marketplace visitor can enumerate holder identities and exact percentages
findings.summary: On U4T22, A2 is neither the listed seller nor a documented owner. Equity Owners nevertheless exposes two full holder identities, exact 51%/2% stakes and Make offer controls. This violates the scenario's explicit private-cap-table boundary.

findings.title: Desktop listing Buy action loses its visible label
findings.summary: The offered-for-sale row renders the Buy action as a small magenta square with no readable label. The browser semantic target is named Buy, but sighted keyboard/mouse users cannot identify the action from the rendered control.

findings.title: One listing has contradictory currencies and magnitudes across marketplace surfaces
findings.summary: U4T22 appears as $10,000 with $50,000 valuation in the catalog, NGN 13,280 with NGN 66,400,000 valuation on detail, then $10 with $0.10 unit price in the modal. A buyer cannot know the actual consideration or valuation before a financial action.

findings.title: Date-picker pointer and keyboard selections do not populate the bid expiry
findings.summary: Selecting future days with pointer and keyboard closed the calendar but left Select Date and Date is required. Manually typing the ISO value populated the control. Human/real-device retest is required after repair.

findings.title: Active listing does not reserve displayed equity and a second over-available listing hangs
findings.summary: After 0.5% of A2's 1% stake persisted as a live listing, both cockpit and detail continued to present the full 1% stake and another Sell action. A second 1%, NGN 2,000 submission remained open without success or error for more than 15 seconds.

findings.title: Seller cannot cancel or revoke an active listing
findings.summary: The exact seller row says Your listing, but exposes no cancel/revoke control. The detail page and cockpit offer only another Sell action, so the required release/cancellation lifecycle cannot be completed.

findings.title: Closure blocker feedback is not itemized or actionable
findings.summary: Admin approval of A1 was blocked only by a generic wallet/pending-balance warning. It supplied no currency, amount, blocking record, status or direct remediation route, so the operator cannot resolve and retest each blocker through the UI.

findings.title: Closed Assessor profile remains actionable
findings.summary: After Admin approved A3's closure and User Management marked the account inactive/closed, its public-profile route still rendered the full profile and enabled Follow. The relationship persisted after refresh, proving downstream actions were not terminally prevented.

findings.title: Closure request and approval produce no in-app or email communication
findings.summary: A3 Notifications contained only account-created/login events after submitting closure. The real inbox contained confirmation, welcome, login-code and later password-reset mail, but no request or approval message.

findings.title: Password-reset email is issued to a closed account
findings.summary: Normal login correctly rejected A3 as blocked/deleted, yet Forgot Password accepted the same identity and delivered a real reset email. The final reset was intentionally not completed; terminal reactivation behavior therefore remains unresolved.

findings.title: Admin closure review note is lost from immutable audit history
findings.summary: The approval event eventually appeared with the correct before/after state, but its reason was No reason recorded even though Admin entered a review note before approval.

findings.title: Image evidence cannot be retained in this runner — screen recording errors on the browser client and host screen capture returns black frames
findings.summary: Image evidence cannot be retained in this runner — screen recording errors on the browser client and host screen capture returns black frames. Cells cannot be signed off on evidence grounds.

findings.title: Accessibility defects on the Assessor Registration form: "+ Add another Industry" is an <h6> heading rather than a button; both chip inputs (#quali…
findings.summary: Accessibility defects on the Assessor Registration form: "+ Add another Industry" is an <h6> heading rather than a button; both chip inputs (#qualification-standard, #award-standard) have no accessible name, only aria-describedby helper text; the industry remove button has no accessible name at all; and both experience selects share the same DOM id mui-component-select-experience, which is invalid HTML and breaks label association.

findings.title: admin row actions are 30px icon-only buttons with aria-label only, rendered below the fold at 1440×900 (y≈1331 in a 900px viewport), so they need s…
findings.summary: The admin row actions are 30px icon-only buttons with aria-label only, rendered below the fold at 1440×900 (y≈1331 in a 900px viewport), so they need scrolling to reach and offer small pointer targets.

findings.title: date-of-birth picker exposes no maximum date — no disabled days, an active next-month arrow and no max on the year input — so future dates are free…
findings.summary: The date-of-birth picker exposes no maximum date — no disabled days, an active next-month arrow and no max on the year input — so future dates are freely selectable and only refused at submit.

findings.title: reason field truncates silently at 250 characters, mid-word, and has no native maxlength, so the limit is JS-only and not exposed to assistive tech
findings.summary: The reason field truncates silently at 250 characters, mid-word, and has no native maxlength, so the limit is JS-only and not exposed to assistive tech.

findings.title: default currency chosen at signup (USD) is not surfaced on the dashboard (amounts masked behind "Show amounts"), so currency persistence to a walle…
findings.summary: The default currency chosen at signup (USD) is not surfaced on the dashboard (amounts masked behind "Show amounts"), so currency persistence to a wallet is not yet verified. Belongs to ASS-029.

findings.title: sell modal gives all three inputs id=outlined-adornment-weight; project has no accessible name and percentage/price are both exposed as weight
findings.summary: The sell modal gives all three inputs id=outlined-adornment-weight; project has no accessible name and percentage/price are both exposed as weight.

findings.title: Login relies on placeholders as the only visible labels and the source of the computed accessible names
findings.summary: Login relies on placeholders as the only visible labels and the source of the computed accessible names. The names are present in the full accessibility tree, but the visual context disappears after entry.

findings.title: Blank recovery-question submission reports only question 1 and duplicates that message inline and as a toast, rather than exposing both missing fie…
findings.summary: Blank recovery-question submission reports only question 1 and duplicates that message inline and as a toast, rather than exposing both missing fields together. Saved questions also are not preselected, so users must rediscover them from lists.

findings.title: Mobile account tab strip does not horizontally scroll
findings.summary: At C-360 only Overview, Profile and part of Manage Assessments are visible. A horizontal-scroll gesture dispatched to the tablist left every tab coordinate unchanged and later account tabs off-screen. The hamburger menu provides an alternative navigation surface, but the required account-tab scrolling behavior is absent.

findings.title: Profile text inputs lack programmatic labels
findings.summary: The C-1280 accessibility snapshot reports empty computed names for First Name, Last Name, City, Alias, primary email and primary phone. The visible label text is not associated programmatically. The empty-required-name state also relies on a red border and disabled Save button without an explanatory inline error, compounding the keyboard/screen-reader failure.

findings.title: Multiple Expertise controls lack accessible names
findings.summary: The profile summary textarea, employment role/employer/date fields, accomplishment title/description/year fields, public-link URL and external-link button, and area-removal buttons expose empty computed names. The employment date picker also announced 2026 month choices while its visible header showed 2025.

findings.title: Public-profile responsive regressions
findings.summary: - C-768 visually omits all 1/1/8 Assessment expertise metric tiles, leaving a blank card body. - C-1024 constrains Assessment Lens to an extremely narrow column, producing a tall word stack and large unused area. - C-360/C-390 repeat G-A9: the account tab strip clips later tabs. The knowledge table itself can be scrolled horizontally to reveal Experience and Proficiency.

findings.title: Assessment rate and currency controls lack useful accessible names
findings.summary: The rate input exposes an empty computed name. The currency select is announced only as its option text (USD NGN) rather than by a persistent Currency label. Visible text is present, but assistive-technology form navigation cannot reliably identify either control.

findings.title: Sensitive KYC fields have empty accessible names
findings.summary: First, middle and last name; date of birth; email; phone; apartment/street/city/postcode; nationality and tax-residency comboboxes; Government ID type input; criminal-history radios; criminal narrative; and sentence radios expose empty or generic computed names. The visible placeholders/nearby text do not provide reliable persistent programmatic labels for assistive-technology form navigation.

findings.title: Viewer sees enabled management actions that effective authorization rejects
findings.summary: The Viewer organization context displayed editable organization profile/KYC controls. Clicking Save with unchanged values produced Organization membership does not grant this permission. and the request returned 403; a fee quote was also rejected. The backend boundary held, but the visible control model does not reflect it and conflicts with the role-label guidance. Unauthorized actions should be hidden/disabled with clear permission copy before submission.

findings.title: Non-owner can reach request builder for another user's pitch
findings.summary: The Pitcher actor did not own UAT Solar Microgrid 73110, yet the Assessment tab rendered enabled Hire Assessor and Request controls and opened the complete request builder. The empty submission path only reported field validation; it did not present an ownership/permission denial. A valid submission was intentionally not attempted because it would contaminate another tester's fixture, so backend authorization remains unproven and requires an isolated retest.

findings.title: Directory close icon has no semantic interactive identity
findings.summary: The visible top-right close icon was absent from the browser's semantic interactive controls and exposed no accessible name. Escape dismissed the dialog, but pointer and assistive-technology users need an actual named close button.

findings.title: Compact directory separates identity from the request action
findings.summary: At 360×844 and 390×844 the table extends far beyond the modal width. Horizontal scrolling exposes the right-side rate and Request action, but removes the name/rating context from view. The row remains technically navigable, yet safe comparison and identity confirmation are not possible in one compact view.

findings.title: Pitch discovery controls expose missing or broken accessible names
findings.summary: The catalogue search input has no accessible name, rating widgets announce null Stars, range sliders have empty names, and the minimum-bid decrement/increment controls are unnamed. These controls are central to discovery and cannot be reliably understood or operated with assistive technology.

findings.title: Advanced-filter taxonomies contain duplicate/default gaps
findings.summary: Funding stage exposes two Any funding stage options; Status exposes both Active and active; and Equity Offered jumps from 31% - 40% to Above 50%, leaving 41%–50% unselectable. These are user-visible query definitions, so duplicates and missing ranges make result interpretation ambiguous.

findings.title: Engagement and restricted-state variants lack isolated fixtures
findings.summary: The only suitable public pitch belongs to another test user. Mutating like/dislike/favourite/follow/comment/report could leave owner notifications or persistent counts on a shared fixture, so those actions were not taken. Private, inactive, deleted, unsupported-country, promoted, related-party and independently known prior-review variants were also unavailable. These branches require isolated seed data and a full rerun.

findings.title: Session confirmation failures make financial commit outcomes ambiguous
findings.summary: During the retry branch the rendered application displayed Unable to confirm your session; Retry remained unavailable, policy acceptance could not load, and logout reported that the server session could not be confirmed. The subsequent login revealed that a request had committed despite the failure state. Stable session confirmation and a definitive success/failure receipt are required before financial submissions can be safely retried.

findings.title: Draft edit icon has no accessible name
findings.summary: The icon at the end of the pitch Assessment summary row reopens the correct reviewId, but its button exposes an empty accessible name. Keyboard/screen-reader users cannot determine its purpose reliably.

findings.title: Task responses and upload surface are not programmatically labelled
findings.summary: All three task textareas and #responseMessage expose empty accessible names even though visible prompt text appears nearby. The visible document drop zone is exposed as a non-interactive div, not a labelled file control. Screen-reader and voice-input users cannot reliably identify the answer target or invoke evidence selection.

findings.title: Review rating and comment controls lack meaningful accessible names
findings.summary: Each star group exposes a generated mui-* name instead of the category plus rating, and all 16 adjacent comment textareas expose empty names. Repeated controls therefore cannot be reliably identified by screen-reader or voice-input users.

findings.title: Repeated RFI controls lack accessible names
