findings.summary: The Title input, response textarea and every per-row action button expose empty accessible names. Users of screen readers or voice input cannot identify the field purpose or distinguish View from Respond actions across repeated rows.

findings.title: RFI table hides essential columns at compact widths
findings.summary: At 360×800 and 390×844, the six-column desktop table overflows its container. Response Time, Due Date and the sole row action begin off-screen, while the page gives no compact-card alternative or visible cue beyond a small horizontal scrollbar. This compounds existing compact account-tab clipping (G-A9).

findings.title: Owner Hires table overlaps the right-side rail at 1440×900
findings.summary: At the desktop control viewport, the due-date, rate and final action columns render underneath the investor-terms/right-menu content. This obscures action affordances in the same view needed to administer temporary access.

findings.title: Compact grant detail overflows and hides the primary action
findings.summary: At 360 and 390 pixels, the title and header action group extend beyond the right edge. At 360, the primary Continue/Apply action lies outside the viewport and horizontal scrolling does not recover it. This is a functional mobile blocker, not cosmetic clipping.

findings.title: Messaging controls lack contextual accessible names
findings.summary: The recipient rows expose two actions both named Chat; the conversation search input, composer and five formatting controls have empty names; and message reaction/reply icon buttons lack message context. Keyboard/pointer operation is possible, but assistive users cannot reliably identify targets.

findings.title: 360-pixel conversation layout clips identity and context
findings.summary: At 360×800, only the right portion of the participant header and context is visible. The name, email and assessment description are cut off beyond the viewport, with no clear horizontal recovery. The composer remains visible but the user cannot reliably verify who or which assessment they are messaging.

findings.title: Notification preference switches have empty accessible names
findings.summary: The four visible switches for Marketing email, Marketing in app, Community email and Community in app can be toggled and persist. Browser accessibility inspection exposes each input with an empty name, so assistive users cannot identify which channel they are changing.

findings.title: Assistant prompt textarea has no accessible name
findings.summary: The visible Assistant composer is keyboard-operable, but browser accessibility inspection exposes the textarea with an empty name, so assistive users cannot identify the field purpose reliably.

findings.title: Secure callback form controls have no accessible names
findings.summary: The form visibly labels Topic, profile phone, summary and consent. Browser accessibility inspection exposes all four corresponding controls with empty names, including the consent checkbox, making the request and privacy-consent flow ambiguous to assistive technology.

findings.title: Marketplace search input has no accessible name
findings.summary: The visible search placeholder is readable, but browser accessibility inspection exposes the input with an empty name.

findings.title: Compact buy table hides essential seller/action content behind horizontal overflow
findings.summary: At 360×800 and 390×844, the live listing table retains desktop width. The seller name is truncated and the action column starts off-screen without a clear responsive alternative.

findings.title: Role keyboard behavior and corrected-error state are inconsistent
findings.summary: With the Assessor role focused, Space did not select it while Enter did. After Enter selected the role, the old Please select role error remained rendered. The role-specific consent error likewise remained after the checkbox was corrected. Evidence: evidence/C-1440/role-space-no-selection.png, role-enter-selected-stale-error.png, ready-to-submit.png.

findings.title: Admin "Unlock Account" did not take effect across three attempts (one returned "Unable to confirm your session")
findings.summary: Admin "Unlock Account" did not take effect across three attempts (one returned "Unable to confirm your session"). The dev API was concurrently failing on /users/session and /users/policyAcceptance, so this is not attributable to the product yet.

findings.title: collaborative browser attachment ended during disposable A3 setup
findings.summary: The collaborative browser attachment ended during disposable A3 setup. The available native Chrome fallback switched key windows when form select menus opened, invalidating it as a safe surface for the destructive terminal branch.

findings.title: A real Assessor holding exists, but the funded buyer, isolated non-owner, active/cancellable listing IDs and immutable ownership/wallet baseline re…
findings.summary: A real Assessor holding exists, but the funded buyer, isolated non-owner, active/cancellable listing IDs and immutable ownership/wallet baseline required for exact settlement are still absent.

findings.title: Collaborative browser was initially unavailable but recovered with screenshot and recording support
findings.summary: Collaborative browser was initially unavailable but recovered with screenshot and recording support.

findings.title: Ownership of the historical Gmail fixture could not be verified
findings.summary: Ownership of the historical Gmail fixture could not be verified. No inbox content was accessed, and the fixture is unsafe for further test use.

findings.title: A valid recovery CTA clicked while already authenticated redirected to Profile rather than opening recovery
findings.summary: A valid recovery CTA clicked while already authenticated redirected to Profile rather than opening recovery.

findings.title: True expiry and two-link supersession were not executable without a documented lifetime or safe token-age/supersession fixture
findings.summary: True expiry and two-link supersession were not executable without a documented lifetime or safe token-age/supersession fixture.

findings.title: Cancelled signup draft persists
findings.summary: Cancel returned to Login, but reopening Sign Up restored the same draft at Security with previously entered personal fields. Expected: Cancel Registration discards the incomplete signup and its personal data, and a later Sign Up starts clean. Impact: prevents a clean restart in the sole profile and retains data contrary to the explicit discard expectation.

findings.title: Owner and public profile scores disagree
findings.summary: the owner profile showed 15 badges and score 419; the public profile for the same actor showed 15 badges and score 100. Expected: the same actor's owner and public profiles present a consistent aggregate badge score, subject only to documented privacy rules. Impact: identity/reputation information is internally inconsistent and may mislead counterparties.

findings.title: Investor is offered a Pitcher signature control
findings.summary: the Investor session visibly exposed both Sign as investor and Sign as pitcher on the draft shareholder agreement. Expected: an Investor can act only as the Investor signatory; Pitcher/entity signature controls are unavailable to that role. Impact: high-risk wrong-role control exposure on a legally significant action. Server-side exploitability was not tested or inferred.

findings.title: Summary counts disagree with empty history lists
findings.summary: UAT Solar showed bid history count 1 with an empty history table; Project Test showed RFI count 1 with an empty RFI table. Current retest on the isolated INV-023 project again showed RFIs 1 with no row for the requesting shareholder; after a separate fixture request was added it showed a global count of 2 while rendering only that actor's one accessible row. A separate PIT2170 accepted-bid history did render, so the list component is not universally empty. Expected: a nonzero history/RFI count has the same number of accessible rows, or the UI clearly explains filtering or unavailable data. Impact: users cannot reach records the product says exist and cannot reconcile lifecycle state.

findings.title: Empty required grant details advance to setup
findings.summary: with all displayed grant details empty, Next advanced to Grant Setup; Back and a second empty Next reproduced the transition. Expected: Next is disabled or blocks progress and identifies every missing required grant detail. Impact: incomplete grant configuration can enter later setup stages without first-step validation.

findings.title: Mobile drawer cannot reach Deactivate Profile
findings.summary: Deactivate Profile was positioned at approximately y=888 below the 844-pixel viewport; scrolling affected the underlying page and did not make the drawer item actionable. Expected: every account control in the mobile navigation drawer is reachable by scroll or another visible control at 390×844. Impact: small-screen users cannot begin account closure through visible navigation.

findings.title: Non-anonymous signup fails on null alias and emits duplicate confirmation mail
findings.summary: submitting complete valid details with anonymous bidding disabled displayed E11000 duplicate key error collection: cicdev1.investors index: alias_1 dup key: { alias: null }. That failed attempt still sent a confirmation message. Enabling anonymous bidding, entering a unique alias and retrying created the account, after which the owned inbox contained two confirmation messages. Expected: the ordinary non-anonymous Investor path accepts no alias, creates one account once, and sends one confirmation message only after successful creation. Failed submissions must not expose internal storage errors or emit account-confirmation mail. Impact: the standard non-anonymous Investor registration path is blocked, an internal database detail is disclosed, and a failed request causes an external email side effect.

findings.title: Notification navigation badge remains stale after mark-read
findings.summary: the page count moved from 11 to 3 and then 0, but the global navigation tab continued to expose Notifications 11 unread notifications. A full browser refresh preserved the mismatch. Navigating away finally cleared the badge. Expected: after page-one and page-two notifications are successfully marked read, the page count and global navigation unread badge reconcile immediately and remain consistent after refresh. Impact: the persistent navigation gives a false unread count and can mislead users into repeatedly checking an empty unread queue.

findings.title: Failed withdrawal does not release its reservation
findings.summary: a NGN 10,000 withdrawal reached Failed; current balance remained NGN 500,000 while available balance remained NGN 490,000 after refresh. A retry added another failed row without releasing the original reservation. Expected: when a withdrawal reaches terminal Failed, its hold is released exactly once so available balance returns to the unchanged current balance. Impact: failed money movement leaves funds unavailable and may strand or cumulatively reserve customer balance.

findings.title: Withdrawal quote total excludes its displayed fee
findings.summary: a NGN 10,000 quote displayed a NGN 53.14 fee but showed total reserved/withdrawal as NGN 10,000; the same flow's validation reasoned about amount plus platform fee, and the failed receipt exposed the fee separately. Expected: displayed amount, fee, total reservation, validation and receipt reconcile to one formula before confirmation. Impact: the user cannot know the actual debit/reservation before authorizing a financial action, and boundary validation may disagree with confirmation copy.

findings.title: Cancelled sessions still offer Join live room
findings.summary: after a dedicated session was cancelled and showed Cancelled/Unavailable, both host and Investor surfaces continued to display Join live room. Expected: a cancelled/unavailable session has no actionable join control, and stale links explain the terminal state without attempting entry. Impact: users are invited to perform an impossible or unauthorized terminal action and may repeatedly attempt to join.

findings.title: Reschedule email converts 30 minutes to 1800 minutes
findings.summary: the owned Mail.tm message body stated 1800 minutes for the rescheduled 30-minute session. Expected: the delivered reschedule message reports the same 30-minute duration shown in the application. Impact: calendar/reminder communication materially misstates meeting length.

findings.title: Distribution form reports no available profit in the wrong currency
findings.summary: while the linked project wallet held USD 1,000, the form displayed Available funds = ₦0 and rejected the attempted payout with Amount exceeds available profits. Expected: the distribution form derives available profit from the linked project wallet and uses its USD currency consistently. Impact: a core return/distribution workflow is blocked or miscomputed despite funded project state.

findings.title: Incoming financial receipts reverse sender and recipient
findings.summary: the Investor dividend receipt labelled the Investor as Sender and project as Recipient; the independently captured USD 5,000 grant receipt labelled applicant Chinedu UAT Okoro as Sender and the grant as Recipient even though the applicant wallet received the credit. Expected: receipts for incoming distribution/grant credits identify the paying project or grant as Sender and the credited user as Recipient. Impact: immutable-looking financial evidence attributes payer/payee backwards, creating audit, support and potential legal/accounting risk.

findings.title: Counteroffer terminates negotiation without an Investor response path
findings.summary: the Pitcher countered the USD 500 / 1% bid to USD 550 / 0.9%. Both actors then saw Countered only in history, the Investor had no response action, and the original USD 500 reservation had already been fully released through release/refund rows. An empty counter submission also produced no visible validation, although it did not mutate the bid. Expected: after a Pitcher counters an Investor bid, the Investor can inspect the revised terms and explicitly accept, reject, or counter; the financial reservation remains deterministic until that branch reaches a terminal outcome. Impact: a core negotiation path cannot proceed after a counter, so users cannot consent to revised economic terms and must create a separate bid to continue.

findings.title: Expired pending bid remains active and keeps funds reserved
findings.summary: after the exact scenario-owned bid passed its seeded near-boundary expiry and the Investor refreshed the rendered application, it still appeared as one active Pending offer. The wallet remained USD 4,800 current and USD 4,550 available, leaving the bid's USD 250 reservation held. Expected: once a pending bid reaches its expiry, refresh/reopen moves it out of active offers, records an auditable expired terminal state, and releases the reservation exactly once. Impact: expired offers remain actionable-looking and strand customer funds, directly blocking reuse or withdrawal of the reserved amount.

findings.title: Pitch preference state is contradictory and Favourites filtering is inaccurate
findings.summary: selecting Dislike while Like was active produced both Unlike pitch and Remove dislike, and a full refresh preserved both reactions. After both reactions were removed and a re-login showed neutral controls, selecting Favourites displayed the complete 33-pitch directory instead of an empty favourite set. Expected: Like and Dislike are mutually exclusive; the active Favourites filter contains only pitches the Investor has favourited/liked and shows an honest empty state after removal. Impact: preference signals can contradict each other and the saved-items directory cannot be trusted for discovery or cleanup.

findings.title: Follow and unfollow totals remain stale until identity handoff
findings.summary: Follow persisted as Unfollow after refresh while the target still showed zero followers. After a later identity handoff the target showed one. Unfollow then persisted as Follow after refresh while the target still showed one; only signing in again as the target reconciled the dashboard to zero. Expected: after Follow or Unfollow succeeds, the target's displayed follower total changes atomically with the persisted action state and stays correct after refresh. Impact: public social proof and owner summaries are visibly wrong during the active session, so users cannot reliably verify whether the mutation reconciled.

findings.title: Successful profile report renders a blank acknowledgement toast
findings.summary: after Submit closed the dialog, the application rendered a toast containing only its close icon and no message. Admin later confirmed exactly one report with the submitted target, reporter and details. Expected: profile-report submission provides a visible, meaningful success or failure acknowledgement so the reporter knows whether to retry. Impact: the reporter receives no usable confirmation and may retry or contact support despite a successful moderation-side write.

findings.title: Investor project wallet falsely displays zero balance and no ledger
findings.summary: each of two accepted shareholders saw USD 0 current/available and an empty project transaction table. The owner of the same project saw USD 945 current/available plus successful USD 1,000 project-funding and USD 55 dividend-payout rows. Expected: an authorized project shareholder can reconcile the project's funded wallet and relevant project ledger against the same project state visible to its owner, subject to documented privacy rules. Impact: both Investors receive a materially false project financial state and cannot reconcile funding or returns. No asset loss or unauthorized transaction was proved, so this is High rather than Critical.

findings.title: Project Equity omits other CIC shareholders and contradicts funded ownership
findings.summary: the 2% shareholder saw own 2% and Other CIC 0%; the 8% shareholder saw own 8% and Other CIC 0%; an unrelated Investor's aggregate view showed CIC 0% and Unallocated 100%. The same project header reported 10% on CIC and two investors. Expected: each authorized viewer sees an internally consistent aggregate capitalization view for the project; the combined CIC percentage reconciles to accepted bids and the project header, while any actor-specific breakdown follows documented privacy rules. Impact: ownership displayed to Investors does not reconcile to the accepted investment state, creating material cap-table and governance uncertainty.

findings.title: Owner cannot create a milestone using selectable valid dates
findings.summary: the owner selected September 12, September 10 and September 11 in separate attempts. Each date rendered in the field, but submission returned Milestone achieved date is required and must be valid; no milestone was created. The future date was correctly disabled, and empty/whitespace title validation worked. Expected: after required text is supplied, a current or earlier selectable achieved date creates exactly one completed milestone and survives refresh. Impact: the owner cannot record a completed delivery through the rendered product, blocking milestone-driven reporting and Investor review.

findings.title: Milestone comment validation and Unicode recovery silently lose input
findings.summary: whitespace closed the dialog with no visible error and created nothing. A valid unique Unicode clarification remained indefinitely in loading and disappeared after reload with zero comments. A later plain-ASCII comment did persist, narrowing the failure to validation/internationalised-input handling rather than all comments. Expected: whitespace is rejected with actionable validation; valid Unicode text submits exactly once or fails recoverably while retaining input; successful comments persist after reload. Impact: Investors can lose substantive internationalised milestone feedback without a deterministic acknowledgement or recoverable draft. ASCII is a workaround for the observed input, so severity is Medium.

findings.title: Owner and unrelated Investor can mutate milestone review state
findings.summary: the owner increased the owner's own Alpha milestone from one to two upvotes. An owned Investor whose Project Holdings list contains no project opened the explicit milestone authorization-test URL, received Support/Push back/Add comment controls, incremented Alpha, and posted a comment that persisted after reload. Signed-out access correctly returned to Login. Expected: project owners cannot vote on their own delivery, and an Investor with no holding or other project relationship cannot create reactions or discussion records on that project's milestones. Impact: unaffiliated users can alter project delivery feedback and owners can inflate approval signals. This is High, not Critical, because this run did not prove a payout, formal acceptance threshold, ownership change or irreversible financial effect.

findings.title: Required milestone delivery and acceptance lifecycle is absent
findings.summary: rendered owner and Investor milestone surfaces exposed only a retrospective Completed milestone title, description and achieved date plus Support, Push back and discussion. No planned/submitted status, progress, evidence, decision or rework control was available. Expected: the project workflow exposes planned/active/late/submitted milestones, progress and delivery evidence, Investor accept/reject/rework decisions, revision history and an auditable terminal state. Impact: the core delivery-review contract in INV-025 cannot be executed, and support/pushback cannot substitute for formal acceptance or rework.

findings.title: Valid project RFI submission is silently lost
findings.summary: the shareholder entered a unique title, valid Unicode description and a visible September 14 due date. Selecting Request closed the dialog as if successful, but no row, confirmation, error or recoverable draft appeared; the list and count remained unchanged after a real reload. Expected: a valid categorized project information request submitted by an authorized shareholder creates exactly one visible request, confirms success or provides recoverable failure, retains its due date/body and survives reload. Impact: an Investor can believe a due-diligence request was lodged when no accessible record exists, blocking accountability and downstream response while losing entered content.

findings.title: Project RFI follow-up, acknowledgment and reopen lifecycle is absent
findings.summary: the co-owner's first response automatically changed the request from Open to Closed. Both co-owner and requesting-Investor detail exposed the original description, one Response section and Back only. No category, follow-up, acknowledgment, rework, manual close, reopen, revision history or audit trail was rendered. Expected: after a project owner responds, the requesting Investor can review the ordered private thread, acknowledge or follow up, explicitly close or request rework, and reopen according to policy; both parties can inspect category, revisions, actors and audit timestamps. Impact: one unilateral response terminates the information-request workflow without Investor acceptance, clarification or rework, so the product cannot evidence that due diligence was satisfactorily resolved.

findings.title: Whitespace-only project RFI response closes and persists blank
findings.summary: the form rejected a truly empty value but accepted spaces only. Selecting Respond closed the dialog, changed the isolated RFI to Closed and rendered an empty Response section. A real reload and requesting-Investor identity handoff preserved the Closed/blank state. Expected: response content is trimmed; empty or whitespace-only input is rejected without changing status, and only a substantive persisted response can advance or close a request. Impact: a responder can falsely mark an Investor due-diligence request resolved without providing information, undermining workflow and audit integrity.

findings.title: Required governance-report obligation, review and revision lifecycle is absent
findings.summary: the owner surface exposed Drafts, History, Trends and Open Questions with Save as Draft and Submit Report. The Investor surface exposed History, Trends, Open Questions and Ask a Question. A v1 report could be read, questioned, replied to and closed, but neither role exposed a due/late obligation, acknowledgement/acceptance, request-correction/rework, create/compare revision, change/audit history, report export or post-close reopen control. Expected: project reporting exposes due and overdue obligations, draft/submitted/revised states, Investor acknowledgement or acceptance, correction/rework, immutable revision comparison and audit history, export, and a recoverable reopen path after closure. Impact: the available discussion path cannot prove that a report was due on time, formally accepted, corrected or superseded. Governance accountability and immutable review completion therefore remain unverifiable.

uniqueFindings.title: Duplicate industries are accepted

uniqueFindings.title: Experience is not cross-validated against date of birth
uniqueFindings.summary: Experience is not cross-validated against date of birth. "60 Years" was accepted for a 41-year-old and stored. With the 18+ rule enforced, no eligible user under ~78 can legitimately hold 60 years of experience, so a public credibility signal is unconstrained.

uniqueFindings.title: Email verification gives no success confirmation — reproduced here on an Assessor identity (third occurrence overall)
uniqueFindings.summary: Email verification gives no success confirmation — reproduced here on an Assessor identity (third occurrence overall).

uniqueFindings.title: No warning before lockout
uniqueFindings.summary: No warning before lockout. Attempts 1–4 give no attempts-remaining hint, so a user with a forgotten password locks themselves out without notice.

uniqueFindings.title: lockout message enumerates accounts
uniqueFindings.summary: The lockout message enumerates accounts. Five wrong-password attempts against any address reveal whether it belongs to a real account: an existing account returns "User account is locked!", while the pre-lock message is deliberately generic. This defeats the non-enumeration posture the login form otherwise maintains and contradicts an explicit requirement of ASS-001 step 2.

uniqueFindings.title: No security notification of any kind is sent when an account is locked — no email and no in-app message
uniqueFindings.summary: No security notification of any kind is sent when an account is locked — no email and no in-app message. The account holder is never informed that their account was locked out, which is the observable signature of a brute-force attempt against them.

uniqueFindings.summary: At 360×800 the role-change dialog's Cancel and Submit render outside the dialog's painted box and outside the viewport, with page scroll locked and neither the dialog nor its container scrollable. Pointer and touch users cannot reach either action; only keyboard Tab recovers them, and a touch device has no Tab key.

uniqueFindings.summary: Submitting a role-change request notifies the requester on no channel — no email, no in-app notification — despite a stated 24-48 hour review window. Approval does send an email, so the gap is specific to submission.

uniqueFindings.summary: Download Data produces a profile snapshot, not a complete portable personal-data export. Data visibly held by CIC—policy acceptance history and preferences—and major account domains are absent.

uniqueFindings.summary: A sensitive personal-data export downloads immediately from an authenticated session without password, MFA or other step-up authentication.

uniqueFindings.summary: Account deactivation Submit becomes enabled with only a reason and static phrase. There is no password/reconfirmation control, so a session thief can initiate closure and the scenario's wrong-password requirement is impossible.

uniqueFindings.title: Sell action is inert for valid partial and full listings
uniqueFindings.summary: The Sell action is inert for valid partial and full listings. Repeated pointer and keyboard submissions produce no progress, success or error, the modal stays open, and the listing count remains zero after refresh.

uniqueFindings.summary: The same owned project's displayed current price changed from $57,900.33 to $0 after refresh and remained $0 after ten seconds, while ownership and portfolio value did not change and no listing/trade was visible.

uniqueFindings.title: Both logged-in Change Password and forgot-password recovery accept a canonical common password that the scenario explicitly requires to be rejected
uniqueFindings.summary: Both logged-in Change Password and forgot-password recovery accept a canonical common password that the scenario explicitly requires to be rejected. The value became a functioning login credential in both paths.

uniqueFindings.title: Forgot-password recovery accepts the account's existing password and reports a successful change, while logged-in Change Password rejects reuse
uniqueFindings.summary: Forgot-password recovery accepts the account's existing password and reports a successful change, while logged-in Change Password rejects reuse. This defeats password-history/current-password protection and emits a misleading security event.

uniqueFindings.title: An explicitly incomplete Assessor can bypass mandatory profile readiness through Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Browse Pitches, open the live as…
uniqueFindings.summary: An explicitly incomplete Assessor can bypass mandatory profile readiness through Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Browse Pitches, open the live assessment editor, save a completely blank draft, and see the server-persisted Draft row afterward. The control is therefore missing at both navigation and mutation boundaries.

uniqueFindings.title: Draft assessment is counted as completed
uniqueFindings.summary: The only authoritative assessment row is Draft, but the Dashboard reports Completed 1, Active Assessments 0, and separately presents the same pitch as pending. This is a direct count/status integrity failure and reproduces at C-360, C-390, C-768, C-1024, C-1280, and C-1440. Impact: assessors and operators cannot trust the dashboard to distinguish unfinished work from completed work. Any completion-based downstream reporting or decisions derived from this card are unsafe.

uniqueFindings.title: Dashboard amount visibility does not survive navigation
uniqueFindings.summary: The explicit Show amounts choice revealed both zero balances and remained after a browser refresh, but after opening Wallet and returning through the visible Overview tab the dashboard reverted to hidden. The safe default is preserved, so this is not a disclosure; it is a preference-persistence failure against the scenario requirement.

uniqueFindings.title: Public-profile entry points do not open the public profile for the current Assessor
uniqueFindings.summary: Both entry points visibly accept input, but the resulting destination is the private role-completion workspace rather than a public profile. This prevents self-preview and blocks the scenario's authenticated-other-role and guest privacy checks. The actor is genuinely missing an expertise area/specialization; ASS-007 will add those through the UI and this finding must then be retested. If the links are intentionally gated, the UI must explain that before presenting them as public-profile actions.

uniqueFindings.title: Invalid experience years persist server-side
uniqueFindings.summary: The specialization accepted and retained -1 years and 999 years after Save Changes and full refresh. The dashboard summary also treated realistic positive values as aggregate experience, while the invalid negative value rendered directly in the card. The API boundary is therefore not enforcing a credible non-negative upper-bounded range. Impact: requester discovery and qualification decisions can be driven by impossible assessor experience claims.

uniqueFindings.title: Expertise catalogue selection can create a mismatched area
uniqueFindings.summary: Choosing the visible Technology menu item produced an area headed Tax with Technology's software/platform description. The actor removed the corrupt row and recreated Technology through the custom-entry field. Impact: assessors can publish a category different from the one selected, corrupting search/discovery and profile interpretation.

uniqueFindings.title: Qualification duplicates are not normalized
uniqueFindings.summary: With CFA already present, a second qualification entered as spaced/lowercase cfa saved and survived refresh. Credentials increased from 1 to 2 and the summary displayed CFA · +1 more. The duplicate was replaced before handoff.

uniqueFindings.title: Impossible accomplishment year persists
uniqueFindings.summary: The accomplishment form accepted 9999; Save Changes succeeded and refresh reproduced the value. The field provides no credible calendar boundary at either client or server persistence layers.

uniqueFindings.title: Employment date picker displays one year and saves another
uniqueFindings.summary: The End Date year input visibly showed 2025, but selecting December produced Dec, 2026. The accessibility snapshot likewise continued naming the month choices as 2026 while the rendered picker header showed 2025. Impact: an assessor can unknowingly publish inaccurate employment dates even after visually selecting the intended year.

uniqueFindings.title: Unsafe javascript: public URL saves and survives refresh
uniqueFindings.summary: The Website URL field accepted javascript:alert(1), returned the normal success toast, and displayed the exact value after a full refresh and accordion reopen. The payload was not executed. A benign HTTPS URL was restored. Impact: every renderer or outbound-link surface must now defensively reject or neutralize this stored value. Server-side allowlisting to https: (and any explicitly supported safe schemes) is required before go-live.

uniqueFindings.title: Alias is ignored on the public profile
uniqueFindings.summary: Bio data labels Alias as “How users see you on the platform” and the saved value persisted as Adebayo-UAT Ω. Every public-profile viewport instead exposes Adebayo Guerrilla-UAT. This defeats the intended public-identity/privacy control and reproduces across all six Chrome sizes.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessment rate has no credible upper bound
uniqueFindings.summary: 999999999999999 produced the normal success confirmation and reloaded as 999,999,999,999,999. This value can therefore enter requester-facing pricing and any downstream financial calculation. Enforce a documented, currency-aware maximum on both client and server.

uniqueFindings.title: Availability and capacity policy cannot be configured
uniqueFindings.summary: The full Account surface exposes only Free/Paid, USD/NGN and rate. There is no availability state, capacity limit, date range, blackout, timezone, conflict, or pause control, and no alternate requestability policy is explained. The earlier #2209 gap remains open, so unavailable or capacity-full behavior cannot be configured or proven.

uniqueFindings.title: KYC has no durable partial-save/resume path
uniqueFindings.summary: Street and postcode remained in the live form across a browser refresh, but Cancel followed by a fresh entry cleared them. There is no Save draft control, saved-progress confirmation, or resume point. A user gathering sensitive evidence across sessions can therefore lose work before the mandatory upload gate.

uniqueFindings.title: Organization context renders personal security notifications
uniqueFindings.summary: After switching A1 into CIC Assessor UAT Ω 2026, the Notifications workspace displayed A1's personal password-reset and password-change history. The active actor was the organization and the scenario explicitly requires notification ownership to follow that actor. This mixes personal security events into a shared institutional context and creates a confidentiality risk for organization members.

uniqueFindings.title: Fresh signup resumes a previous tester's identity draft
uniqueFindings.summary: Opening the signup flow for a new isolated email on the same collaborative browser reached a confirmation page populated with another tester's name, email and phone (UATClosure Assessor, an uberip.com address and a different phone). The values were visible before correction. This is persistent registration-data remanence across test identities on a shared browser and can expose one applicant's PII to the next person using the device.

uniqueFindings.title: Keyboard expertise selection displays the filter without applying it
uniqueFindings.summary: Mouse-selecting Accounting produced no eligible rows. After clearing, typing the same value into the same control and choosing it with ArrowDown/Enter produced the same input text and matching-filter banner but left Uat assessor visible. The directory therefore presents two materially different eligibility result sets for an identical visible filter state. This breaks keyboard access and makes search results untrustworthy.

uniqueFindings.title: Directory omits required readiness, capacity and profile evidence
uniqueFindings.summary: The only result exposed a generic name, zero rating, country, an unlabeled type icon, Not provided specialization, Free, and Request. It had no public-profile link, availability/capacity state, KYC/readiness indication, expertise evidence summary, industry match, or reason for eligibility. The required free/paid and converted-currency comparison is also absent. Requesters cannot make or audit the decision this scenario requires.

uniqueFindings.title: Request handoff loses the selected Assessor identity
uniqueFindings.summary: After Request was clicked on Uat assessor, the assessment form did not display the Assessor's name, alias, profile, specialization, readiness or directory rate. A requester cannot verify that the scope is being sent to the intended person, violating the scenario's exact-identity handoff requirement and increasing misrouting risk.

uniqueFindings.title: Minimum Accepted Bids accepts a negative filter value
uniqueFindings.summary: The advanced numeric filter retained -1 with no validation message or normalization and returned the unfiltered six-pitch set. A minimum-count constraint cannot be negative; accepting it creates an invalid visible query state and unreliable filter semantics.

uniqueFindings.title: Unverified/KYC-incomplete Assessor is offered volunteer review despite an existing pitch relationship
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 displayed both the Unverified badge and Complete your KYC requirements, while the dashboard already showed a separate Requestor pending assessment for UAT Solar Microgrid 73110. The same pitch nevertheless exposed enabled Write Free Review. The scenario explicitly requires incomplete-profile/KYC, already-hired and conflict variants to be blocked before draft creation or recovery.

uniqueFindings.title: Existing volunteer draft is hidden until Write Free Review is clicked
uniqueFindings.summary: Before the action, the Assessment table was empty and the UI offered Write Free Review. Clicking it immediately replaced that state with a Draft/You row. Opening the row showed the same review ID had last been saved at 02:34:17, well before this run. Existing work must be surfaced as Resume/Edit on initial load; presenting a creation action for hidden state makes duplicate/conflict behavior impossible to reason about.

uniqueFindings.title: Dashboard omits the volunteer draft shown in Manage Assessments
uniqueFindings.summary: Manage Assessments displayed the pitch as a free Draft and the pitch Assessment row persisted it after refresh. The dashboard still reported Active Assessments 0 and surfaced only a different Requestor pending card for that pitch. This fails the scenario's traceable-draft requirement and gives the Assessor conflicting work queues.

uniqueFindings.title: Ambiguous retry creates a duplicate paid request instead of reconciling one intent
uniqueFindings.summary: After the first request was known successful, P1 deliberately reopened the identical form to exercise retry protection. The first click in that retry attempt disabled the Request button; a rapid second click could not target the disabled control. The app then reported it could not confirm the session, making the retry outcome ambiguous. After login/reload, two identical paid rows existed in P1 Hires, A1 dashboard, A1 Requests and A1 Notifications. The server must reject/reconcile equivalent in-flight or recent retries with an idempotency boundary and return an unambiguous outcome. A duplicate second wallet hold is plausible but was not counted as proven because the wallet view could not be recovered before role change.

uniqueFindings.title: Request CTAs lose object identity and open unrelated default work
uniqueFindings.summary: Both the in-app Open notification action and the actual email's View the request link navigated to /manage-assessments with no request identifier. The workspace defaulted to the Assessments tab and unrelated volunteer work; the Assessor had to discover the Requests tab and infer which indistinguishable row was intended. This also prevented request-specific wrong-account, expiry, deleted/private pitch and missing-object authorization checks.

uniqueFindings.title: Real email shifts response deadlines one calendar day earlier
uniqueFindings.summary: The paid request displayed 15 September 2026 in both requester and Assessor UI, but its email stated 14 September. The free request displayed 16 September in the UI, but its inbox preview stated 15 September. Reproducing the same -1 day error on consecutive dates is consistent with an incorrect timezone/date-only conversion and can cause premature expiry or missed contractual response windows.

uniqueFindings.title: Free request email is described as a paid-assessment request
uniqueFindings.summary: The free variant was published and submitted at NGN 0.00, and the in-app notification correctly displayed that amount. Its real-email subject/preview nevertheless said You have a new paid-assessment request. The message misstates the commercial nature of the request even while presenting a zero fee.

uniqueFindings.title: Durable request, notification and email counts diverge
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 retained three request rows/cards and three corresponding in-app notifications: two paid duplicates and one free request. The actual mailbox contained only two emails, one for the paid requester/pitch and one for the free requester/pitch. Exactly-once delivery is broken in opposite directions across channels, leaving no reliable audit trail for which committed financial request was communicated.

uniqueFindings.title: Investor requester's Hires view does not reconcile its successful request
uniqueFindings.summary: I1 submitted the free request successfully and A1 immediately received the resulting card and notification. Returning to the same pitch's Hires tab as I1 produced no row after tab toggling and reload. The requester therefore cannot confirm or manage the request it created. I1 was also acting on a P1-owned pitch because the application exposed Hire Assessor to the non-owner Investor, repeating G-A16 from ASS-011.

uniqueFindings.title: Decision dialog omits essential request identity and commercial context
uniqueFindings.summary: The Requests table contained requester, status, response deadline, due date and fee, but Accept/Reject reduced the decision to pitch title, delivery date, fee and tasks. It omitted requester identity, assessment type, response deadline, current status and explicit currency code. A1 therefore cannot verify the complete request inside the very surface where irreversible acceptance/rejection occurs. The free Review comparator had the same omissions.

uniqueFindings.title: Scope and request-document workflows are absent
uniqueFindings.summary: The non-Review request builder exposed only 1–3 task text fields; there was no scope, requester note, attachment, public/private classification, or permitted pitch-document selector. The A1 decision surface offered no scope, attachment list, pitch/deck link, preview or download action. Consequently no public/private/removed-file authorization, safe filename/content-type, or least-privilege document decision can be made through the product.

uniqueFindings.title: Legal documents cannot support versioned, auditable consent
uniqueFindings.summary: Both documents were readable, but neither displayed a version, publication/effective date, governing-policy identifier or supersession marker. A checkbox submission can therefore record only a generic boolean from the visible workflow, not which terms were presented and accepted. This prevents a reliable legal audit trail when content changes.

uniqueFindings.title: Duplicate tasks are accepted without detection or clarification
uniqueFindings.summary: P1 entered the exact same 92-character task twice. The request submitted successfully, Edit preserved both values, and A1 was required to check two visually identical obligations. The builder should either prevent exact duplicates or require the requester to disambiguate them so completion evidence maps to a unique obligation.

uniqueFindings.title: Zero-task validation remains after the form is corrected
uniqueFindings.summary: After the empty submission, the form displayed an actionable zero-task error. Adding three non-empty tasks did not clear that error; it remained visible next to 92/250, 92/250 and 250/250 counters until the successful submission removed the dialog. Stale error state makes a corrected request appear invalid and undermines recovery feedback.

uniqueFindings.title: Accepted requests are stranded outside the Assessor workspaces
uniqueFindings.summary: Both Requests rows became Accepted, but A1's dashboard continued to show Active Assessments 0. Manage Assessments → Assessments showed only an unrelated historical volunteer draft, Assigned Projects showed zero items, and the accepted dashboard card routed back to generic Requests without a response action. The request-specific response form exists and works when A1 is manually given the requester-side URL, so this is a discovery/assignment-integration failure that prevents normal delivery.

uniqueFindings.title: Requesters can open the Assessor's editable submission form
uniqueFindings.summary: While visibly authenticated as P1, the real paid acceptance email CTA and the matching in-app notification opened the Technology Assessment Response form with all requested tasks, comment fields, attachment upload and Submit Assessment. Independently, I1's free acceptance notification opened the editable Review Assessment Response form. A requester must never receive authorization to author or upload the Assessor's deliverable. Server-side submission authorization was not destructively probed in ASS-015 and must be covered by the dedicated authorization retest.

uniqueFindings.title: Free acceptance communications claim a zero-value wallet hold
uniqueFindings.summary: I1's in-app notification and real email say NGN 0.00 has been reserved from your wallet; the email then says that this fee is held until the assessment is completed. The free request created no wallet transaction, so the communication invents a financial operation and can confuse the requester. Free acceptance content should explicitly state that no charge or reservation was made.

uniqueFindings.title: Rejection is an unconfirmed one-click action with no required reason
uniqueFindings.summary: The Reject dialog accepted an empty Notes field and its Reject button immediately committed the terminal state. There was no explicit confirmation/review step, no opportunity to cancel after the destructive click, and no reason was shown in the requester notification/email or retained in the visible terminal record. Accidental or unexplained rejection therefore cannot be distinguished or audited.

uniqueFindings.title: One rejection is represented as two positive wallet reversals and rewrites the original hold
uniqueFindings.summary: P1's available balance correctly increased once by NGN 25,000, but wallet history added a new positive Refund row while changing the original negative assessment hold into another positive declined/Cancelled reservation-release row that retained the old hold reference. A financial audit cannot reconstruct the original reservation and sees two apparent credits for one balance movement. Reservation and reversal must be immutable, separately referenced entries whose signed amounts reconcile exactly to the displayed balance.

uniqueFindings.title: Requester cancellation removes the record but leaves NGN 25,000 locked
uniqueFindings.summary: The unlabeled Hires action committed cancellation in one click without confirmation or reason. The request disappeared from both role workspaces instead of persisting as Cancelled, no notification/email was delivered, and P1's available balance did not recover: the NGN 25,000 hold remained in the wallet. This both strands requester funds and eliminates the user-visible audit trail.

uniqueFindings.title: Response-deadline expiry is not enforced and expired requests can be accepted
uniqueFindings.summary: After their stored response deadlines passed, requests remained Pending and actionable, with holds still locked and no Expired state or communication. Acceptance succeeded from both a dialog opened before the boundary and an independent dialog opened only after expiry; each persisted Accepted after reload and generated an acceptance email. The UI exposes only a calendar date without a time, timezone or countdown, but the fresh-dialog result establishes a server-backed lifecycle failure rather than merely ambiguous display copy.

uniqueFindings.title: Incoming paid-request emails were not delivered to the Assessor
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 received both requests in-app, but the actual Guerrilla Mail inbox never received either A16E1 or A16E2 incoming-request email. Earlier request emails remained visible, demonstrating mailbox continuity. Missing delivery removes the required off-platform prompt for time-sensitive response deadlines.

uniqueFindings.title: Negative rates are silently converted into positive proposals
uniqueFindings.summary: Typing -100 removed the minus sign, displayed 100 and enabled Send Proposal. A destructive financial input must be rejected with clear inline feedback, not transformed into a materially different valid offer.

uniqueFindings.title: Proposal input has no defensible upper bound or affordability guard
uniqueFindings.summary: A 20-digit NGN amount was formatted normally and left Send Proposal enabled with no maximum, warning or confirmation. This creates fat-finger and abuse exposure far beyond the requester's wallet and ordinary assessment values.

uniqueFindings.title: Negotiation notes are double-escaped across application and email
uniqueFindings.summary: The submitted < character rendered as the literal text < for A1, P1 and the real email. Notes otherwise persisted, so this is a consistent presentation/encoding defect rather than input loss.

uniqueFindings.title: Proposal success can be reported without durable persistence
uniqueFindings.summary: Two A17E NGN 40,000 submissions displayed a success toast while the request stayed Pending at NGN 25,000 after refresh. A later clean-session NGN 42,000 retry persisted. Success must not be announced until the durable state is confirmed, and idempotent recovery must make the final outcome unambiguous.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessor-authored rates are mislabeled as client proposals
uniqueFindings.summary: After A17A acceptance and A17R rejection, A1's own Requests cards labeled the value Client proposed rate. The requester did not author either proposal. This reverses negotiation authorship in the audit presentation.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessor does not receive rate-outcome notifications or complete email delivery
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 received the requests in-app, but no acceptance/rejection outcome appeared after P1 responded. Its real mailbox received neither the three A17 incoming-request emails nor any rate outcome email, while P1's proposal notifications/emails arrived. Time-sensitive negotiation cannot rely on one-sided delivery.

uniqueFindings.title: Request copy misstates when funds are committed
uniqueFindings.summary: The requester modal says funds are committed only after the final negotiated rate is accepted, yet submitting each base-rate request immediately created an NGN 25,000 reservation hold. The financial copy must accurately explain the initial reservation and later delta adjustment.

uniqueFindings.title: Date-only assessment terms shift one day earlier in actual emails
uniqueFindings.summary: The live UI showed A18E's proposed due date as 6 October 2026, while P1's delivered counter-offer email showed 5 October. The same email retained the Assessor's prose saying 6 October, making it internally contradictory. Separately, A18A's response deadline displayed as 20 September in the app but 19 September in A1's request email. Date-only commercial deadlines must use one documented timezone/calendar representation in every channel.

uniqueFindings.title: Request search omits visible Unicode, rate and assessment-type data
uniqueFindings.summary: The queue contained Ω in every pitch title, yet searching Ω returned no matches. Searching the visible NGN value 25,000 also returned none. Searching Review returned only two A17 rows even though known Review records exceed that result. Exact title, requester and status searches passed, demonstrating that the control works but indexes an inconsistent subset of the work-item model.

uniqueFindings.title: Search is neither debounced nor programmatically named
uniqueFindings.summary: Typing leaves the previous result set unchanged until Enter is pressed, contrary to the scenario's debounced-loading requirement. The visible Search placeholder does not provide an accessible name: the live input was exposed with an empty name. Add an explicit label/accessible name, defined submit behavior if intended, loading announcement, and consistent keyboard/pointer behavior.

uniqueFindings.title: Request workspace drops due-date negotiation rationale
uniqueFindings.summary: A18E was accepted after a due-date-only proposal with a submitted reason, but the request queue labelled its note control No negotiation note. A18A contained separate due-date and rate reasons, yet the queue dialog showed only the rate text. Assessors cannot reconstruct why the operative due date changed from this primary work queue.

uniqueFindings.title: Assignment sub-navigation changes URL/highlight but keeps the assessment form
uniqueFindings.summary: From a valid saved-draft route, selecting Overview, Pitch Deck or Information Request updates the sidebar highlight and changes tab=1, tab=5 or tab=6. The page body nevertheless remains the editable Assessment rubric. The Assessor cannot obtain the required source context, evidence or Q&A from this contracted-work shell, and route state no longer describes rendered content.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessment search is case- and whitespace-sensitive
uniqueFindings.summary: The exact identifier P7SUN returned the saved row, but p7sun and p7sun both produced the no-match state. This differs from the Requests workspace, where lowercase and padded title variants passed in ASS-019. Normalize case and surrounding whitespace consistently before searching.

uniqueFindings.title: Organization context can directly load the personal actor's editable draft
uniqueFindings.summary: After switching to the organization actor, its assessment list correctly showed zero records. The personal P7SUN draft nevertheless stayed fully editable in the already-open route, and refreshing the same reviewId URL in organization context loaded the full editable rubric again. Context-aware authorization/list visibility disagree, creating an attribution and cross-context data-integrity risk.

uniqueFindings.title: Logout discards the active assignment return route
uniqueFindings.summary: Logging out from the saved draft navigated to bare /login. Logging back in as A1 reached /dashboard, not the assessment. Direct guest access does provide a protected-pitch interstitial whose Log in link carries the complete returnUrl, so the continuity capability exists but is not used by explicit logout.

uniqueFindings.title: Non-Review assessment answers cannot be saved and are lost on refresh
uniqueFindings.summary: The Technology response page offers only Submit Assessment. It has no Save draft, autosave state, unsaved-change warning or recovery path. After valid independent answers made Submit ready, refreshing the exact assignment route reset every task comment and the overall assessment to zero. A multi-task professional assessment cannot safely be completed over more than one sitting.

uniqueFindings.title: Structured tasks collapse to untyped comments without contract context
uniqueFindings.summary: The accepted assignment exposes only prompt text and a minimum-50-character textarea per task. It omits required/optional status, answer type, helper text, response/due deadlines, accepted rate/currency, requester, aggregate progress and dependency behavior. The upstream request UI also provided no way to author numeric, choice, boolean, date, URL or conditional tasks. The planned structured-task contract therefore cannot be represented end to end.

uniqueFindings.title: Review validation is bottom-only and does not focus invalid fields
uniqueFindings.summary: Both empty and partial Submit actions leave the viewport at the top with no inline guidance. A combined error appears only below the entire 16-row rubric, and it reports All assessment scores rather than identifying individual categories. Keyboard and screen-reader users receive no focus movement to the first problem.

uniqueFindings.title: Recommendation options are bidding tactics rather than assessment conclusions
uniqueFindings.summary: The required Recommendation field offers equity bargaining and timing tactics, including delaying a bid until the last minute for bargaining power. The values do not define a neutral conclusion such as recommend, recommend with conditions, request more evidence or do not recommend, so a professional assessment cannot record a clear independent outcome.

uniqueFindings.title: The 1–5 rubric has no scale definitions
uniqueFindings.summary: Sixteen unrelated categories use the same stars, but the page provides no label for what 1 versus 5 means, whether a higher score is always better, or evidence thresholds. Assessors cannot apply the rubric consistently and requesters cannot interpret the aggregate reliably.

uniqueFindings.title: Completed Review submits irreversibly without confirmation
uniqueFindings.summary: Activating Submit on a fully populated review immediately persisted it and displayed success. There is no confirmation dialog, final read-only summary, acknowledgement of requester visibility, or cancel window despite the absence of any later edit action in the canonical submitted viewer.

uniqueFindings.title: Submitted review's original draft URL still exposes Save and Submit
uniqueFindings.summary: The canonical submitted viewer is read-only, but navigating back to the exact reviewId URL used before submission renders an empty editable rubric with Save as draft and Submit. This breaks terminal-state enforcement at the UI boundary and exposes duplicate/overwrite risk. The actual second-submit outcome is carried into ASS-025.

uniqueFindings.title: Submitted assessment has a blank Status cell
uniqueFindings.summary: After the volunteer review persisted and the dashboard labelled it completed, the Manage Assessments row showed title, three-star rounded rating, date and Free charge but no Status value. Users cannot distinguish draft, submitted or other terminal states from the authoritative work list.

uniqueFindings.title: Empty and unchanged draft saves have no dirty-state guard
uniqueFindings.summary: Save as draft accepts a completely empty Review and remains enabled immediately after acknowledgement. Activating it again with no changes performs another save and updates the saved state without explaining whether a version was created. The UI provides no dirty, saving, unchanged or version indicator to prevent redundant writes or communicate what changed.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessments-list resume opens an incompatible form and strands rubric data
uniqueFindings.summary: The authoritative saved-work row is correctly labelled Draft, but activating its title opens Review Assessment Response, a generic single 0/5000-character answer. It contains none of the saved 16 category ratings/comments, four selects or Notes. The request queue's Continue assessment route still restores the rubric, so the data exists but the documented list/dashboard resume path sends the Assessor to the wrong editor.

uniqueFindings.title: Stale tab silently overwrites newer draft fields
uniqueFindings.summary: Two tabs loaded the same saved baseline. Tab B saved a newer row 1 rating/comment and Notes. Tab A, without reloading, changed only row 8 and saved later. No conflict/version warning appeared. Reloading proved tab B's independent newer values were replaced by tab A's stale baseline while tab A's row 8 edit won. The draft service therefore applies last-write-wins to the whole record and silently loses acknowledged professional work.

uniqueFindings.title: Navigation discards unsaved draft edits without warning
uniqueFindings.summary: After changing Notes, activating the account Overview tab immediately navigated to Dashboard. There was no confirmation, before-leave prompt, autosave or recovery notice. Reopening the assignment restored only the previous saved Note, proving the unsaved edit was discarded.

uniqueFindings.title: Exact duplicate RFIs are accepted as independent requests
uniqueFindings.summary: After one RFI was durably visible, A1 reopened the composer and submitted the exact same title, description and due date. The table immediately contained two indistinguishable Open rows. There was no warning, merge behavior or idempotency protection, so a retry can create duplicate obligations and conflicting closure histories.

uniqueFindings.title: RFI creation and response produce no in-app notification or email
uniqueFindings.summary: P1's notification badge remained 15 and its real YOPmail inbox remained 18 after two RFI creations. After P1 answered, A1's badge remained at its pre-run baseline of 24, the newest notification page contained only older assessment-request events, and its real Guerrilla Mail inbox contained no RFI response. Neither actor receives a CTA/deep link for time-sensitive Q&A.

uniqueFindings.title: Whitespace response can close an RFI with blank persisted content
uniqueFindings.summary: The owner composer displayed Response Message Cannot be empty for whitespace. Without any later valid submission on that first row, it then became Closed/On Time. Opening the detail as both P1 and A1 showed an empty Response. The system therefore commits a state the client says is invalid, irreversibly closes the request and loses the required answer.

uniqueFindings.title: RFI is a one-shot close, not an auditable Q&A lifecycle
uniqueFindings.summary: Open detail omits assignment/request identity, requester, status, due date and timestamps. Sending the first response automatically closes the record; closed detail provides no responder identity, response timestamp, attachment history, acknowledgement, explicit close, correction, follow-up or reopen control. The requester and Assessor cannot manage clarification or establish who did what when.

uniqueFindings.title: Later valid RFI submissions silently disappear
uniqueFindings.summary: After both initial RFIs were closed, A1 twice entered a new title, valid description and future due date. Each Request action dismissed the composer, but no success or error appeared and the count stayed at two after waiting and refresh. If a maximum exists it is undisclosed; otherwise valid work is silently lost.

uniqueFindings.title: Final Review accepts an assessment with almost every category comment blank
uniqueFindings.summary: The form says Please fill out all fields, yet the paid Review became terminal with valid scores and only two of 16 category comments. Both Assessor and requester canonical viewers show 14 em dashes. A supposedly complete professional deliverable can therefore omit nearly all written justification, and the contract presented to the user contradicts the enforced contract.

uniqueFindings.title: Completed paid Review remains reserved with no observed settlement path
uniqueFindings.summary: A18A changed to Completed and exposed its final 1.56 output, but P1's NGN 25,000 and NGN 13,000 entries remained Reservation Holds, P1 available balance remained NGN 210,000, and A1 available balance remained zero. Unlike Technology, the Review output exposed no Pay Now/Need More Time/Dispute panel. The NGN 38,000 engagement is terminal in work state but not financially finalizable from the reached UI.

uniqueFindings.title: Final assessment completion is not delivered in app or by email
uniqueFindings.summary: Neither A18A Review nor A14T1 Technology generated a completion notification for the requester or Assessor, and neither real test mailbox received a completion message. A1 received an in-app event only after P1 manually paid Technology; no payment email reached either mailbox. Users cannot reliably discover a deliverable or retain off-platform delivery proof.

uniqueFindings.title: Technology Task 2 persists Task 1's answer
uniqueFindings.summary: Task 1 and Task 2 intentionally used the same prompt but received distinct answers and distinct pre-submit counters (118 and 119 characters). The terminal response shown to both P1 and A1 repeats Task 1's 118-character answer under Task 2. Task 2's submitted answer is lost, corrupting the signed-off professional output.

uniqueFindings.title: Successful Technology capture removes value from the Assessor balance
uniqueFindings.summary: P1's NGN 25,000 payment correctly reduced requester current balance from NGN 500,000 to NGN 475,000 and changed the reservation to Capture/Success. A1's corresponding +NGN 25,000 ledger row also says Reservation Capture/Success and produced a paid notification, but A1 current balance fell from NGN 290,000 to NGN 265,000 while available balance stayed NGN 0. The UI therefore reports a successful payer debit and recipient credit event while making the recipient NGN 25,000 worse off and providing no spendable earnings.

uniqueFindings.title: No explicit post-submission rework lifecycle exists
uniqueFindings.summary: Requester P1 can read both terminal types and see Completed Hires, but there is no Request revision/Rework action, reason dialog, pending state, cancel, duplicate prevention, accept/reject decision or assessor work item. Technology chat becomes read-only after payout; Review exposes only ordinary chat. A correction therefore cannot be initiated through a permissioned, auditable workflow, so every reason, notification, rework-edit, resubmission and resolution branch in this scenario is unreachable.

uniqueFindings.title: Terminal assessments have no version identity or revision audit surface
uniqueFindings.summary: The canonical Review and Technology views show content and author, but no version number, immutable original identifier, submitted/finalized timestamps, change history, requested-change scope, comparison or attachment lineage. Even if support manually changed data, users could not distinguish the signed original from a correction or audit who finalized which version.

uniqueFindings.title: UI declares an overdue hold released while the wallet remains reserved
uniqueFindings.summary: A18E was more than 80 hours past its due time. Both roles rendered Deadline Missed and Auto-failed; hold released, and the Assessor could no longer save. Nevertheless, P1's NGN 25,000 reservation remained pending and available balance did not increase after the lifecycle window. A financial terminal state must not be announced before its settlement commits, and the scheduler must idempotently release the hold.

uniqueFindings.title: Pending requester holds contaminate the Assessor current balance
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 current balance fell NGN 265,000→240,000 when an unpaid held request was terminated, then returned to NGN 265,000 when P1 created a new NGN 25,000 held request. A1 available balance remained zero throughout. The Assessor's current balance therefore includes money that has neither been paid nor made available, and termination appears to debit the Assessor. Pending escrow must be represented separately from owned/current funds.

uniqueFindings.title: One termination release is represented twice and its receipt reverses the money direction
uniqueFindings.summary: P1 correctly regained NGN 25,000 available once, but the history shows both a new positive Refund row and the original reservation mutated into a positive Reservation Release row. The new refund receipt then labels P1 as Sender and Assessor as Recipient even though the funds returned to P1. The ledger must retain an immutable negative hold plus one clearly linked release/refund, with correct sender/recipient semantics.

uniqueFindings.title: Requester cancellation/termination is unavailable outside the late window
uniqueFindings.summary: Before lateness, an accepted Hires row exposed only chat. After submission, the Technology record exposed payment, extension and dispute controls but no cancellation/termination action. Terminate appeared only after the seeded late state. The product therefore cannot execute or audit the required pre-start, in-progress and post-submission cancellation branches.

uniqueFindings.title: Deadline, auto-fail and termination events send no in-app or email communication
uniqueFindings.summary: Neither A18E's auto-fail claim nor A18R's committed termination produced an A1 notification or real email. No reminder or exact boundary message was observed. Adverse financial lifecycle changes need role-appropriate in-app and email delivery with a valid, authorized link.

uniqueFindings.title: Dispute alert has no usable Assessor response or record deep link
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 received a correct notification and real email, but both links landed on generic /manage-assessments. The NGN 25,000 assessment row had a blank Status. Opening the exact submission showed no Filed badge, dispute type, reason, timestamp, evidence or Respond/Acknowledge action; only the ordinary chat became read-only. The email explicitly instructs the Assessor to respond through the platform, which is impossible. P1 also received no filing confirmation in app or email, and no administration decision/audit surface was exposed.

uniqueFindings.title: Eligible requesters cannot rate completed Assessor work
uniqueFindings.summary: P1 owns completed paid Review and Technology engagements with A1, including one fully paid Technology output. Neither canonical output, Hires row, profile nor Feedback center exposes a requester-to-Assessor score/comment action. There is no prior rating indicator or edit policy. Every required authorization, numeric-boundary, long/unsafe comment, cancel, duplicate and stale-tab rating check is therefore impossible, and A1 cannot accrue reputation from delivered work.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessor reputation has no auditable aggregate or rating history
uniqueFindings.summary: The request directory renders A1 as (0), every Manage Assessments My Rating cell is blank, and the authenticated public profile renders badges/score but no rating average, count, comments, engagement link or rating history. Users cannot distinguish unrated from zero-rated, reconcile directory/profile/list state, or verify arithmetic. Badge score 25 is a different metric and is not labelled as an assessment rating.

uniqueFindings.title: Report workflows are inconsistent and provide no durable reporter audit trail
uniqueFindings.summary: The Q&A Report action commits immediately with no reason, target summary, confirmation or cancel and becomes only Already reported. Report profile has a reason and optional details plus Cancel, but after submit the profile simply returns with Report profile still enabled. Neither report appears in the Feedback status center or creates a reporter notification/email. Target non-notification can protect reporter privacy, but the submitting user cannot retain a receipt, reference or moderation status.

uniqueFindings.title: Reciprocal settled receipts disagree on payer/payee direction
uniqueFindings.summary: P1's receipt for the NGN 25,000 A14T1 capture identifies Ngozi as Sender and Assessor as Recipient. A1's corresponding receipt identifies Adebayo as Sender, Requestor as Recipient and Requestor as Provider. Both say settled transfer and net recipient NGN 25,000, but cannot both describe the same money direction. This makes the audit document unreliable even before comparing the broken balances.

uniqueFindings.title: Linked financial-account UI is not credibly user-scoped or usable for payout
uniqueFindings.summary: Two isolated users display the exact same USD/NGN/GBP bank aliases, masked account suffix 0123 and four Spending Card suffixes/06/23 expiry dates. A1's withdrawal payout selector nevertheless says No options. The account page therefore exposes fixture-like financial data as if linked to each personal profile while not producing a selectable payout account.

uniqueFindings.title: Approved-KYC Assessor cannot configure or complete any withdrawal
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 is visibly KYC Valid, but NGN withdrawal says NGN bank payouts available and NGN payout setup unavailable in the same dialog. Add payout account only redirects back to this dead end. With no selectable account, valid/minimum/maximum withdrawal, confirmation, idempotency and every pending/success/failure/reversal state are unreachable.

uniqueFindings.title: Wallet sort controls are inert
uniqueFindings.summary: Date and Amount are exposed as clickable table-header controls. Starting from the same ten-row A1 page, two Date clicks and one Amount click left the row order unchanged and exposed no ascending/descending indicator. Search, filters and pagination work, so this is isolated to sorting.

uniqueFindings.title: Active Assessor project is absent from Assigned Projects
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 has a working temporary-access route, appears in the owner's roster and can see its accepted hire. Assigned Projects nevertheless reports zero rows. An exact-title search returns no match, leaving the Assessor dependent on a guessed or externally supplied URL.

uniqueFindings.title: Temporary Assessor can read exact project-wallet balances
uniqueFindings.summary: The temporary-access project exposes NGN 100,000 available, NGN 25,000 pending/held and NGN 125,000 current. The scenario requires the wallet and bank/account controls to remain hidden or denied; this is direct financial-data disclosure outside the assignment's assessment scope.

uniqueFindings.title: Completed/ended engagement retains private read/write project access
uniqueFindings.summary: A1's completed A14T1 engagement still opens the project and private ended-phase milestone without a temporary-access banner. The Assessor successfully changed the milestone from zero to one Support vote, and the mutation survived a full refresh. Post-boundary access is therefore neither read-only nor revoked.

uniqueFindings.title: Organization actor inherits a personal assignment's milestone access
uniqueFindings.summary: After switching from A1 Personal into an organization with zero assigned projects, a direct A16E1 milestone URL still rendered the personal assignment's private milestone and write controls. The temporary-access banner disappeared, so the application both loses the contracted actor identity and keeps the underlying personal authorization.

uniqueFindings.title: Project RFI has no owner response or communications lifecycle
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 can create an RFI and P1 can read it, but the owner detail has no answer/response action. No new owner notification was present and the real test inbox remained unchanged after refresh. The persisted open RFI is therefore operationally stranded.

uniqueFindings.title: Milestone comment submission silently loses valid content
uniqueFindings.summary: The comment modal accepted long Unicode and harmless HTML-like text. Post comment closed the modal, but immediate and refreshed milestone views remained at zero comments/discussions and no error explained the loss.

uniqueFindings.title: Project owner cannot revoke displayed temporary access
uniqueFindings.summary: The owner roster explains the temporary grant and expiry, while Hires shows the accepted engagement. Neither exposes revoke, end access, cancel or equivalent control, so immediate removal cannot be performed through the authorized owner UI.

uniqueFindings.title: Schedule commits while the browser reports insufficient credit
uniqueFindings.summary: Submitting the P1 schedule form left the modal open with Insufficient session credit, yet the exact session already existed in the browser list and opened normally. A host can retry a committed action because the UI represents success as failure.

uniqueFindings.title: Session communications corrupt timezone and duration
uniqueFindings.summary: The product page showed 13:05 local while the schedule communication showed 12:05. Reschedule communications repeated the one-hour offset. A 1,800-second duration was labelled 1800 minutes instead of 30 minutes. These errors can make participants miss the live event.

uniqueFindings.title: Session invitation and membership authorization are absent
uniqueFindings.summary: There is no invite/remove control or membership roster. A fresh unrelated Assessor and an unrelated Investor could open future, live and ended session URLs, receive Participant permissions, enter live rooms and read persisted chat/recording metadata. Access is effectively possession of the URL plus any logged-in account.

uniqueFindings.title: Cancelled session exposes an active join path and live room
uniqueFindings.summary: After P1 confirmed cancellation, the session page displayed Unavailable but retained Join live room. Uninvited A2 clicked it and entered a room labelled SESSION IN PROGRESS, so cancellation does not close the live authorization boundary.

uniqueFindings.title: Participant capacity and queue are not enforced
uniqueFindings.summary: The fixture visibly identified itself as a one-seat capacity prerequisite. A1, A2 and unrelated I1 all entered; the participant panel showed three people and no waiting, queue, admission or rejection state.

uniqueFindings.title: Host entry auto-starts without required prejoin and device workflow
