uniqueFindings.summary: Opening at the boundary immediately marked the session in progress. There was no explicit Start confirmation, camera/microphone preview, device selector, no-device branch or hand-raise control. Permission failures were either raw Agora errors or silent control resets.

uniqueFindings.title: Leave and participant presence become mutually inconsistent
uniqueFindings.summary: Navigating away did not warn or promptly remove A1 from P1's roster. Explicit Leave told A1 the session had ended and exposed processed-recording copy while P1 remained live; P1 retained the stale participant. A1 could rejoin afterward.

uniqueFindings.title: Chat, reply, report and ended-state controls are unreliable
uniqueFindings.summary: A1's top-level message reached P1 only after reload. Reply submit cleared without creating a reply, Report gave no feedback, Like changed ordering, and the ended session kept an enabled composer whose submits silently disappeared. Although literal HTML-like text was safely escaped, the collaboration and audit trail are not reliable.

uniqueFindings.title: Completion summaries misstate participants and end time
uniqueFindings.summary: The room showed two participants, the host completion communication said one, and the pitch card said zero. The card displayed scheduled end instead of actual host-confirmed end. Usage reconciliation therefore cannot be trusted as a faithful session record.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessor lifecycle communications are incomplete
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 received no completion, reschedule or cancellation event/email and has no session history/directory. At the reminder boundary A1 and A2 each got one correct in-app reminder and deep link, but neither real inbox received a reminder by 14:05.

uniqueFindings.title: Host lifecycle communications have wrong identity/content and broken CTA
uniqueFindings.summary: Cancellation messaging tells the host they registered interest in their own session, reschedule content omits useful time/duration in app, emails carry the timezone/duration corruption, and the cancellation email CTA opens the application homepage rather than the session.

uniqueFindings.title: Fresh Assessor transactional email does not arrive
uniqueFindings.summary: A2 completed browser signup and requested resend/login delivery. The product reported success and created matching in-app verification/login notifications, but the visibly refreshed YOPmail inbox remained empty. P1's inbox on the same provider received session lifecycle mail during this run, so this is not treated as a provider-wide evidence outage.

uniqueFindings.title: Eligibility filter includes a deliberately ineligible grant
uniqueFindings.summary: A2 visibly contradicts the seed's Male, Aerospace Manufacturing and Canada/Ontario requirements. Eligible for you still leaves that grant in the catalogue. This makes the filter unsafe for applicant decision-making and agrees with the later server-enforcement failure.

uniqueFindings.title: Invalid custom URL fails without applicant-facing feedback
uniqueFindings.summary: Submitting notaurl in the optional URL answer leaves the modal open after a failed request, but no field error, toast or recovery instruction appears. The applicant cannot distinguish validation failure from a frozen submit.

uniqueFindings.title: Application decision notification has no deep-link action
uniqueFindings.summary: The rejected applicant receives correct public feedback in-app, but that event exposes no Open notification control. The actual email does provide a working View grant link, making delivery behavior inconsistent across channels.

uniqueFindings.title: Draft invitation exposes Join and returns a generic server error
uniqueFindings.summary: An invited Assessor sees the draft private grant and a functioning-looking Join modal. Final Join produces only Internal Server Error. The UI should suppress Join until the grant is joinable or explain the owner action required.

uniqueFindings.title: Fixed co-grantor invitation falsely states that funds will be deducted
uniqueFindings.summary: The private invitation required no contribution and A1 had zero available funds. The modal nevertheless stated that NGN 75,000 would be deducted. This is materially misleading financial consent copy even though no contribution was actually recorded.

uniqueFindings.title: Anonymous co-grantor identity leaks across owner channels
uniqueFindings.summary: A1 selected Join anonymously. P1's Grantors table, in-app acceptance event and actual acceptance email all identify Adebayo Guerrilla-UAT. The option promises name privacy from grantors/applicants but does not enforce it for the creator-facing downstream state.

uniqueFindings.title: Grantors tab count is zero while two members are listed
uniqueFindings.summary: Both A1 and P1 views display Grantors (0) above a table containing the creator and A1. The count cannot be relied on for membership/reconciliation.

uniqueFindings.title: Closed grant keeps active Apply flow
uniqueFindings.summary: The guest page visibly says Closed with a past deadline yet keeps Apply and Fund active. Apply routes through Login and opens the full application modal for A2. The server correctly rejects Submit and Save Draft, but users are invited into an impossible workflow.

uniqueFindings.title: Closed catalogue filter returns open grants
uniqueFindings.summary: After selecting Closed, the headline changes to Explore closed grants, but the eligible, review and ineligible ASS-032 grants—each visibly open—remain in the result set. Status discovery is not trustworthy.

uniqueFindings.title: Server accepts an application from an ineligible Assessor
uniqueFindings.summary: The deliberately ineligible grant lists three criteria contradicted by A2. The UI opens Apply and the server accepts the completed application, which persists as Already Applied. Eligibility is neither communicated accurately nor enforced.

uniqueFindings.title: Literal HTML-shaped message content is silently discarded
uniqueFindings.summary: The composer accepted literal <script>…</script>, no code executed, but both tags and the enclosed inert text disappeared from the rendered message. Sanitization is effective against execution but changes user-authored content without warning.

uniqueFindings.title: Unsent chat draft is lost on refresh
uniqueFindings.summary: An exact Unicode draft was visible in the composer before refresh. Reopening the same conversation returned an empty composer with no recovery notice.

uniqueFindings.title: Long unbroken message overflows the conversation viewport
uniqueFindings.summary: A 1,536-character unbroken token inside a 1,577-character message persisted but extended beyond the message bubble instead of wrapping, hiding content horizontally.

uniqueFindings.title: Cancelled assessment conversation remains writable
uniqueFindings.summary: The request workspace labels the Accounting request Cancelled. Its assessment conversation still exposes an enabled composer and accepted ASS-033 post-termination message should be blocked Ω; the message remained after refresh. The failed/deadline-missed variant correctly becomes read-only, proving the lifecycle policy is inconsistent.

uniqueFindings.title: Completed assessment has no chat entry point
uniqueFindings.summary: The completed Technology assessment renders in Manage Assessments but its six-column row contains no action or chat control. The required completed-assignment communication path cannot be reached through the UI.

uniqueFindings.title: System-created assessment context is labelled as the Assessor's message
uniqueFindings.summary: The automatically generated This conversation was created for the Review assessment... event is rendered with Your message. That misattributes system provenance and weakens the chat's audit semantics.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessment request chat actions begin outside the desktop viewport
uniqueFindings.summary: At 1440×900, the Requests table initially ends at the deadline/status columns. Chat/actions sit beyond the right edge and only appear after scrolling the table horizontally, making the primary workflow undiscoverable at a standard desktop width.

uniqueFindings.title: Global unread badge remains stale after page-level read state reaches zero
uniqueFindings.summary: After opening individual events and then using Mark page as read, the Notifications page persisted zero unread and rendered the correct empty Unread state. The global account-tab badge still showed five through a full refresh. Only logout/login removed it. This leaves users with contradictory notification state and can cause repeated, fruitless checks for unread work.

uniqueFindings.title: Enabled feedback launcher is absent, blocking every feedback submission branch
uniqueFindings.summary: Feedback says the movable launcher is visible on every page and its setting successfully toggles off/on. With the setting on, fully loaded Dashboard, Manage Assessments and Wallet pages expose no launcher or submission control. A user therefore cannot create even a basic feedback report, and the expected status/admin lifecycle has no originating record.

uniqueFindings.title: Assistant reports irrelevant answers as 95% high-confidence grounded help
uniqueFindings.summary: The safe navigation prompt explicitly asked how to reach the Assessor dashboard and assigned assessments. The response instead defined roles, wallets and grants, while displaying High confidence, 95% and Grounded answer. Citations are present but do not make the response useful for the requested task.

uniqueFindings.title: Assistant support handoff reports success without creating an actionable handoff
uniqueFindings.summary: Contact support shows Support handoff requested, but it neither navigates nor returns a correlation reference. Opening Support immediately afterward shows no active session or handoff-created request. Users can reasonably believe a human escalation exists when none is visible.

uniqueFindings.title: Assistant omits privacy refusal and irreversible-action safeguards
uniqueFindings.summary: Requests for another user's private assessment data and for immediate account closure/fund withdrawal both receive unrelated 95% high-confidence generic answers. No private data was disclosed and no write occurred, but the product does not state the privacy boundary, refuse the request or warn that irreversible financial/account actions require confirmation.

uniqueFindings.title: Assistant silently truncates long prompts before persistence
uniqueFindings.summary: The 1,534-character prompt was fully visible before send. Its persisted audit retains the start and only 148 of 180 repeated tokens; the explicit end marker is absent. There is no visible maximum, counter, validation or truncation warning, yet the Assistant answers the incomplete value.

uniqueFindings.title: Unrelated marketplace visitor can enumerate holder identities and exact percentages
uniqueFindings.summary: On U4T22, A2 is neither the listed seller nor a documented owner. Equity Owners nevertheless exposes two full holder identities, exact 51%/2% stakes and Make offer controls. This violates the scenario's explicit private-cap-table boundary.

uniqueFindings.title: Desktop listing Buy action loses its visible label
uniqueFindings.summary: The offered-for-sale row renders the Buy action as a small magenta square with no readable label. The browser semantic target is named Buy, but sighted keyboard/mouse users cannot identify the action from the rendered control.

uniqueFindings.title: One listing has contradictory currencies and magnitudes across marketplace surfaces
uniqueFindings.summary: U4T22 appears as $10,000 with $50,000 valuation in the catalog, NGN 13,280 with NGN 66,400,000 valuation on detail, then $10 with $0.10 unit price in the modal. A buyer cannot know the actual consideration or valuation before a financial action.

uniqueFindings.title: Date-picker pointer and keyboard selections do not populate the bid expiry
uniqueFindings.summary: Selecting future days with pointer and keyboard closed the calendar but left Select Date and Date is required. Manually typing the ISO value populated the control. Human/real-device retest is required after repair.

uniqueFindings.title: Active listing does not reserve displayed equity and a second over-available listing hangs
uniqueFindings.summary: After 0.5% of A2's 1% stake persisted as a live listing, both cockpit and detail continued to present the full 1% stake and another Sell action. A second 1%, NGN 2,000 submission remained open without success or error for more than 15 seconds.

uniqueFindings.title: Seller cannot cancel or revoke an active listing
uniqueFindings.summary: The exact seller row says Your listing, but exposes no cancel/revoke control. The detail page and cockpit offer only another Sell action, so the required release/cancellation lifecycle cannot be completed.

uniqueFindings.title: Closure blocker feedback is not itemized or actionable
uniqueFindings.summary: Admin approval of A1 was blocked only by a generic wallet/pending-balance warning. It supplied no currency, amount, blocking record, status or direct remediation route, so the operator cannot resolve and retest each blocker through the UI.

uniqueFindings.title: Closed Assessor profile remains actionable
uniqueFindings.summary: After Admin approved A3's closure and User Management marked the account inactive/closed, its public-profile route still rendered the full profile and enabled Follow. The relationship persisted after refresh, proving downstream actions were not terminally prevented.

uniqueFindings.title: Closure request and approval produce no in-app or email communication
uniqueFindings.summary: A3 Notifications contained only account-created/login events after submitting closure. The real inbox contained confirmation, welcome, login-code and later password-reset mail, but no request or approval message.

uniqueFindings.title: Password-reset email is issued to a closed account
uniqueFindings.summary: Normal login correctly rejected A3 as blocked/deleted, yet Forgot Password accepted the same identity and delivered a real reset email. The final reset was intentionally not completed; terminal reactivation behavior therefore remains unresolved.

uniqueFindings.title: Admin closure review note is lost from immutable audit history
uniqueFindings.summary: The approval event eventually appeared with the correct before/after state, but its reason was No reason recorded even though Admin entered a review note before approval.

uniqueFindings.title: Image evidence cannot be retained in this runner — screen recording errors on the browser client and host screen capture returns black frames
uniqueFindings.summary: Image evidence cannot be retained in this runner — screen recording errors on the browser client and host screen capture returns black frames. Cells cannot be signed off on evidence grounds.

uniqueFindings.title: Accessibility defects on the Assessor Registration form: "+ Add another Industry" is an <h6> heading rather than a button; both chip inputs (#quali…
uniqueFindings.summary: Accessibility defects on the Assessor Registration form: "+ Add another Industry" is an <h6> heading rather than a button; both chip inputs (#qualification-standard, #award-standard) have no accessible name, only aria-describedby helper text; the industry remove button has no accessible name at all; and both experience selects share the same DOM id mui-component-select-experience, which is invalid HTML and breaks label association.

uniqueFindings.title: admin row actions are 30px icon-only buttons with aria-label only, rendered below the fold at 1440×900 (y≈1331 in a 900px viewport), so they need s…
uniqueFindings.summary: The admin row actions are 30px icon-only buttons with aria-label only, rendered below the fold at 1440×900 (y≈1331 in a 900px viewport), so they need scrolling to reach and offer small pointer targets.

uniqueFindings.title: date-of-birth picker exposes no maximum date — no disabled days, an active next-month arrow and no max on the year input — so future dates are free…
uniqueFindings.summary: The date-of-birth picker exposes no maximum date — no disabled days, an active next-month arrow and no max on the year input — so future dates are freely selectable and only refused at submit.

uniqueFindings.title: reason field truncates silently at 250 characters, mid-word, and has no native maxlength, so the limit is JS-only and not exposed to assistive tech
uniqueFindings.summary: The reason field truncates silently at 250 characters, mid-word, and has no native maxlength, so the limit is JS-only and not exposed to assistive tech.

uniqueFindings.title: default currency chosen at signup (USD) is not surfaced on the dashboard (amounts masked behind "Show amounts"), so currency persistence to a walle…
uniqueFindings.summary: The default currency chosen at signup (USD) is not surfaced on the dashboard (amounts masked behind "Show amounts"), so currency persistence to a wallet is not yet verified. Belongs to ASS-029.

uniqueFindings.title: sell modal gives all three inputs id=outlined-adornment-weight; project has no accessible name and percentage/price are both exposed as weight
uniqueFindings.summary: The sell modal gives all three inputs id=outlined-adornment-weight; project has no accessible name and percentage/price are both exposed as weight.

uniqueFindings.title: Login relies on placeholders as the only visible labels and the source of the computed accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: Login relies on placeholders as the only visible labels and the source of the computed accessible names. The names are present in the full accessibility tree, but the visual context disappears after entry.

uniqueFindings.title: Blank recovery-question submission reports only question 1 and duplicates that message inline and as a toast, rather than exposing both missing fie…
uniqueFindings.summary: Blank recovery-question submission reports only question 1 and duplicates that message inline and as a toast, rather than exposing both missing fields together. Saved questions also are not preselected, so users must rediscover them from lists.

uniqueFindings.title: Mobile account tab strip does not horizontally scroll
uniqueFindings.summary: At C-360 only Overview, Profile and part of Manage Assessments are visible. A horizontal-scroll gesture dispatched to the tablist left every tab coordinate unchanged and later account tabs off-screen. The hamburger menu provides an alternative navigation surface, but the required account-tab scrolling behavior is absent.

uniqueFindings.title: Profile text inputs lack programmatic labels
uniqueFindings.summary: The C-1280 accessibility snapshot reports empty computed names for First Name, Last Name, City, Alias, primary email and primary phone. The visible label text is not associated programmatically. The empty-required-name state also relies on a red border and disabled Save button without an explanatory inline error, compounding the keyboard/screen-reader failure.

uniqueFindings.title: Multiple Expertise controls lack accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The profile summary textarea, employment role/employer/date fields, accomplishment title/description/year fields, public-link URL and external-link button, and area-removal buttons expose empty computed names. The employment date picker also announced 2026 month choices while its visible header showed 2025.

uniqueFindings.title: Public-profile responsive regressions
uniqueFindings.summary: - C-768 visually omits all 1/1/8 Assessment expertise metric tiles, leaving a blank card body. - C-1024 constrains Assessment Lens to an extremely narrow column, producing a tall word stack and large unused area. - C-360/C-390 repeat G-A9: the account tab strip clips later tabs. The knowledge table itself can be scrolled horizontally to reveal Experience and Proficiency.

uniqueFindings.title: Assessment rate and currency controls lack useful accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The rate input exposes an empty computed name. The currency select is announced only as its option text (USD NGN) rather than by a persistent Currency label. Visible text is present, but assistive-technology form navigation cannot reliably identify either control.

uniqueFindings.title: Sensitive KYC fields have empty accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: First, middle and last name; date of birth; email; phone; apartment/street/city/postcode; nationality and tax-residency comboboxes; Government ID type input; criminal-history radios; criminal narrative; and sentence radios expose empty or generic computed names. The visible placeholders/nearby text do not provide reliable persistent programmatic labels for assistive-technology form navigation.

uniqueFindings.title: Viewer sees enabled management actions that effective authorization rejects
uniqueFindings.summary: The Viewer organization context displayed editable organization profile/KYC controls. Clicking Save with unchanged values produced Organization membership does not grant this permission. and the request returned 403; a fee quote was also rejected. The backend boundary held, but the visible control model does not reflect it and conflicts with the role-label guidance. Unauthorized actions should be hidden/disabled with clear permission copy before submission.

uniqueFindings.title: Non-owner can reach request builder for another user's pitch
uniqueFindings.summary: The Pitcher actor did not own UAT Solar Microgrid 73110, yet the Assessment tab rendered enabled Hire Assessor and Request controls and opened the complete request builder. The empty submission path only reported field validation; it did not present an ownership/permission denial. A valid submission was intentionally not attempted because it would contaminate another tester's fixture, so backend authorization remains unproven and requires an isolated retest.

uniqueFindings.title: Directory close icon has no semantic interactive identity
uniqueFindings.summary: The visible top-right close icon was absent from the browser's semantic interactive controls and exposed no accessible name. Escape dismissed the dialog, but pointer and assistive-technology users need an actual named close button.

uniqueFindings.title: Compact directory separates identity from the request action
uniqueFindings.summary: At 360×844 and 390×844 the table extends far beyond the modal width. Horizontal scrolling exposes the right-side rate and Request action, but removes the name/rating context from view. The row remains technically navigable, yet safe comparison and identity confirmation are not possible in one compact view.

uniqueFindings.title: Pitch discovery controls expose missing or broken accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The catalogue search input has no accessible name, rating widgets announce null Stars, range sliders have empty names, and the minimum-bid decrement/increment controls are unnamed. These controls are central to discovery and cannot be reliably understood or operated with assistive technology.

uniqueFindings.title: Advanced-filter taxonomies contain duplicate/default gaps
uniqueFindings.summary: Funding stage exposes two Any funding stage options; Status exposes both Active and active; and Equity Offered jumps from 31% - 40% to Above 50%, leaving 41%–50% unselectable. These are user-visible query definitions, so duplicates and missing ranges make result interpretation ambiguous.

uniqueFindings.title: Engagement and restricted-state variants lack isolated fixtures
uniqueFindings.summary: The only suitable public pitch belongs to another test user. Mutating like/dislike/favourite/follow/comment/report could leave owner notifications or persistent counts on a shared fixture, so those actions were not taken. Private, inactive, deleted, unsupported-country, promoted, related-party and independently known prior-review variants were also unavailable. These branches require isolated seed data and a full rerun.

uniqueFindings.title: Session confirmation failures make financial commit outcomes ambiguous
uniqueFindings.summary: During the retry branch the rendered application displayed Unable to confirm your session; Retry remained unavailable, policy acceptance could not load, and logout reported that the server session could not be confirmed. The subsequent login revealed that a request had committed despite the failure state. Stable session confirmation and a definitive success/failure receipt are required before financial submissions can be safely retried.

uniqueFindings.title: Draft edit icon has no accessible name
uniqueFindings.summary: The icon at the end of the pitch Assessment summary row reopens the correct reviewId, but its button exposes an empty accessible name. Keyboard/screen-reader users cannot determine its purpose reliably.

uniqueFindings.title: Task responses and upload surface are not programmatically labelled
uniqueFindings.summary: All three task textareas and #responseMessage expose empty accessible names even though visible prompt text appears nearby. The visible document drop zone is exposed as a non-interactive div, not a labelled file control. Screen-reader and voice-input users cannot reliably identify the answer target or invoke evidence selection.

uniqueFindings.title: Review rating and comment controls lack meaningful accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: Each star group exposes a generated mui-* name instead of the category plus rating, and all 16 adjacent comment textareas expose empty names. Repeated controls therefore cannot be reliably identified by screen-reader or voice-input users.

uniqueFindings.title: Repeated RFI controls lack accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The Title input, response textarea and every per-row action button expose empty accessible names. Users of screen readers or voice input cannot identify the field purpose or distinguish View from Respond actions across repeated rows.

uniqueFindings.title: RFI table hides essential columns at compact widths
uniqueFindings.summary: At 360×800 and 390×844, the six-column desktop table overflows its container. Response Time, Due Date and the sole row action begin off-screen, while the page gives no compact-card alternative or visible cue beyond a small horizontal scrollbar. This compounds existing compact account-tab clipping (G-A9).

uniqueFindings.title: Owner Hires table overlaps the right-side rail at 1440×900
uniqueFindings.summary: At the desktop control viewport, the due-date, rate and final action columns render underneath the investor-terms/right-menu content. This obscures action affordances in the same view needed to administer temporary access.

uniqueFindings.title: Compact grant detail overflows and hides the primary action
uniqueFindings.summary: At 360 and 390 pixels, the title and header action group extend beyond the right edge. At 360, the primary Continue/Apply action lies outside the viewport and horizontal scrolling does not recover it. This is a functional mobile blocker, not cosmetic clipping.

uniqueFindings.title: Messaging controls lack contextual accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The recipient rows expose two actions both named Chat; the conversation search input, composer and five formatting controls have empty names; and message reaction/reply icon buttons lack message context. Keyboard/pointer operation is possible, but assistive users cannot reliably identify targets.

uniqueFindings.title: 360-pixel conversation layout clips identity and context
uniqueFindings.summary: At 360×800, only the right portion of the participant header and context is visible. The name, email and assessment description are cut off beyond the viewport, with no clear horizontal recovery. The composer remains visible but the user cannot reliably verify who or which assessment they are messaging.

uniqueFindings.title: Notification preference switches have empty accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The four visible switches for Marketing email, Marketing in app, Community email and Community in app can be toggled and persist. Browser accessibility inspection exposes each input with an empty name, so assistive users cannot identify which channel they are changing.

uniqueFindings.title: Assistant prompt textarea has no accessible name
uniqueFindings.summary: The visible Assistant composer is keyboard-operable, but browser accessibility inspection exposes the textarea with an empty name, so assistive users cannot identify the field purpose reliably.

uniqueFindings.title: Secure callback form controls have no accessible names
uniqueFindings.summary: The form visibly labels Topic, profile phone, summary and consent. Browser accessibility inspection exposes all four corresponding controls with empty names, including the consent checkbox, making the request and privacy-consent flow ambiguous to assistive technology.

uniqueFindings.title: Marketplace search input has no accessible name
uniqueFindings.summary: The visible search placeholder is readable, but browser accessibility inspection exposes the input with an empty name.

uniqueFindings.title: Compact buy table hides essential seller/action content behind horizontal overflow
uniqueFindings.summary: At 360×800 and 390×844, the live listing table retains desktop width. The seller name is truncated and the action column starts off-screen without a clear responsive alternative.

uniqueFindings.title: Role keyboard behavior and corrected-error state are inconsistent
uniqueFindings.summary: With the Assessor role focused, Space did not select it while Enter did. After Enter selected the role, the old Please select role error remained rendered. The role-specific consent error likewise remained after the checkbox was corrected. Evidence: evidence/C-1440/role-space-no-selection.png, role-enter-selected-stale-error.png, ready-to-submit.png.

uniqueFindings.title: Admin "Unlock Account" did not take effect across three attempts (one returned "Unable to confirm your session")
uniqueFindings.summary: Admin "Unlock Account" did not take effect across three attempts (one returned "Unable to confirm your session"). The dev API was concurrently failing on /users/session and /users/policyAcceptance, so this is not attributable to the product yet.

uniqueFindings.title: collaborative browser attachment ended during disposable A3 setup
uniqueFindings.summary: The collaborative browser attachment ended during disposable A3 setup. The available native Chrome fallback switched key windows when form select menus opened, invalidating it as a safe surface for the destructive terminal branch.

uniqueFindings.title: A real Assessor holding exists, but the funded buyer, isolated non-owner, active/cancellable listing IDs and immutable ownership/wallet baseline re…
uniqueFindings.summary: A real Assessor holding exists, but the funded buyer, isolated non-owner, active/cancellable listing IDs and immutable ownership/wallet baseline required for exact settlement are still absent.

uniqueFindings.title: Collaborative browser was initially unavailable but recovered with screenshot and recording support
uniqueFindings.summary: Collaborative browser was initially unavailable but recovered with screenshot and recording support.

uniqueFindings.title: Ownership of the historical Gmail fixture could not be verified
uniqueFindings.summary: Ownership of the historical Gmail fixture could not be verified. No inbox content was accessed, and the fixture is unsafe for further test use.

uniqueFindings.title: A valid recovery CTA clicked while already authenticated redirected to Profile rather than opening recovery
uniqueFindings.summary: A valid recovery CTA clicked while already authenticated redirected to Profile rather than opening recovery.

uniqueFindings.title: True expiry and two-link supersession were not executable without a documented lifetime or safe token-age/supersession fixture
uniqueFindings.summary: True expiry and two-link supersession were not executable without a documented lifetime or safe token-age/supersession fixture.

uniqueFindings.title: Cancelled signup draft persists
uniqueFindings.summary: Cancel returned to Login, but reopening Sign Up restored the same draft at Security with previously entered personal fields. Expected: Cancel Registration discards the incomplete signup and its personal data, and a later Sign Up starts clean. Impact: prevents a clean restart in the sole profile and retains data contrary to the explicit discard expectation.

uniqueFindings.title: Owner and public profile scores disagree
uniqueFindings.summary: the owner profile showed 15 badges and score 419; the public profile for the same actor showed 15 badges and score 100. Expected: the same actor's owner and public profiles present a consistent aggregate badge score, subject only to documented privacy rules. Impact: identity/reputation information is internally inconsistent and may mislead counterparties.

uniqueFindings.title: Investor is offered a Pitcher signature control
uniqueFindings.summary: the Investor session visibly exposed both Sign as investor and Sign as pitcher on the draft shareholder agreement. Expected: an Investor can act only as the Investor signatory; Pitcher/entity signature controls are unavailable to that role. Impact: high-risk wrong-role control exposure on a legally significant action. Server-side exploitability was not tested or inferred.

uniqueFindings.title: Summary counts disagree with empty history lists
uniqueFindings.summary: UAT Solar showed bid history count 1 with an empty history table; Project Test showed RFI count 1 with an empty RFI table. Current retest on the isolated INV-023 project again showed RFIs 1 with no row for the requesting shareholder; after a separate fixture request was added it showed a global count of 2 while rendering only that actor's one accessible row. A separate PIT2170 accepted-bid history did render, so the list component is not universally empty. Expected: a nonzero history/RFI count has the same number of accessible rows, or the UI clearly explains filtering or unavailable data. Impact: users cannot reach records the product says exist and cannot reconcile lifecycle state.

uniqueFindings.title: Empty required grant details advance to setup
uniqueFindings.summary: with all displayed grant details empty, Next advanced to Grant Setup; Back and a second empty Next reproduced the transition. Expected: Next is disabled or blocks progress and identifies every missing required grant detail. Impact: incomplete grant configuration can enter later setup stages without first-step validation.

uniqueFindings.title: Mobile drawer cannot reach Deactivate Profile
uniqueFindings.summary: Deactivate Profile was positioned at approximately y=888 below the 844-pixel viewport; scrolling affected the underlying page and did not make the drawer item actionable. Expected: every account control in the mobile navigation drawer is reachable by scroll or another visible control at 390×844. Impact: small-screen users cannot begin account closure through visible navigation.

uniqueFindings.title: Non-anonymous signup fails on null alias and emits duplicate confirmation mail
uniqueFindings.summary: submitting complete valid details with anonymous bidding disabled displayed E11000 duplicate key error collection: cicdev1.investors index: alias_1 dup key: { alias: null }. That failed attempt still sent a confirmation message. Enabling anonymous bidding, entering a unique alias and retrying created the account, after which the owned inbox contained two confirmation messages. Expected: the ordinary non-anonymous Investor path accepts no alias, creates one account once, and sends one confirmation message only after successful creation. Failed submissions must not expose internal storage errors or emit account-confirmation mail. Impact: the standard non-anonymous Investor registration path is blocked, an internal database detail is disclosed, and a failed request causes an external email side effect.

uniqueFindings.title: Notification navigation badge remains stale after mark-read
uniqueFindings.summary: the page count moved from 11 to 3 and then 0, but the global navigation tab continued to expose Notifications 11 unread notifications. A full browser refresh preserved the mismatch. Navigating away finally cleared the badge. Expected: after page-one and page-two notifications are successfully marked read, the page count and global navigation unread badge reconcile immediately and remain consistent after refresh. Impact: the persistent navigation gives a false unread count and can mislead users into repeatedly checking an empty unread queue.

uniqueFindings.title: Failed withdrawal does not release its reservation
uniqueFindings.summary: a NGN 10,000 withdrawal reached Failed; current balance remained NGN 500,000 while available balance remained NGN 490,000 after refresh. A retry added another failed row without releasing the original reservation. Expected: when a withdrawal reaches terminal Failed, its hold is released exactly once so available balance returns to the unchanged current balance. Impact: failed money movement leaves funds unavailable and may strand or cumulatively reserve customer balance.

uniqueFindings.title: Withdrawal quote total excludes its displayed fee
uniqueFindings.summary: a NGN 10,000 quote displayed a NGN 53.14 fee but showed total reserved/withdrawal as NGN 10,000; the same flow's validation reasoned about amount plus platform fee, and the failed receipt exposed the fee separately. Expected: displayed amount, fee, total reservation, validation and receipt reconcile to one formula before confirmation. Impact: the user cannot know the actual debit/reservation before authorizing a financial action, and boundary validation may disagree with confirmation copy.

uniqueFindings.title: Cancelled sessions still offer Join live room
uniqueFindings.summary: after a dedicated session was cancelled and showed Cancelled/Unavailable, both host and Investor surfaces continued to display Join live room. Expected: a cancelled/unavailable session has no actionable join control, and stale links explain the terminal state without attempting entry. Impact: users are invited to perform an impossible or unauthorized terminal action and may repeatedly attempt to join.

uniqueFindings.title: Reschedule email converts 30 minutes to 1800 minutes
uniqueFindings.summary: the owned Mail.tm message body stated 1800 minutes for the rescheduled 30-minute session. Expected: the delivered reschedule message reports the same 30-minute duration shown in the application. Impact: calendar/reminder communication materially misstates meeting length.

uniqueFindings.title: Distribution form reports no available profit in the wrong currency
uniqueFindings.summary: while the linked project wallet held USD 1,000, the form displayed Available funds = ₦0 and rejected the attempted payout with Amount exceeds available profits. Expected: the distribution form derives available profit from the linked project wallet and uses its USD currency consistently. Impact: a core return/distribution workflow is blocked or miscomputed despite funded project state.

uniqueFindings.title: Incoming financial receipts reverse sender and recipient
uniqueFindings.summary: the Investor dividend receipt labelled the Investor as Sender and project as Recipient; the independently captured USD 5,000 grant receipt labelled applicant Chinedu UAT Okoro as Sender and the grant as Recipient even though the applicant wallet received the credit. Expected: receipts for incoming distribution/grant credits identify the paying project or grant as Sender and the credited user as Recipient. Impact: immutable-looking financial evidence attributes payer/payee backwards, creating audit, support and potential legal/accounting risk.

uniqueFindings.title: Counteroffer terminates negotiation without an Investor response path
uniqueFindings.summary: the Pitcher countered the USD 500 / 1% bid to USD 550 / 0.9%. Both actors then saw Countered only in history, the Investor had no response action, and the original USD 500 reservation had already been fully released through release/refund rows. An empty counter submission also produced no visible validation, although it did not mutate the bid. Expected: after a Pitcher counters an Investor bid, the Investor can inspect the revised terms and explicitly accept, reject, or counter; the financial reservation remains deterministic until that branch reaches a terminal outcome. Impact: a core negotiation path cannot proceed after a counter, so users cannot consent to revised economic terms and must create a separate bid to continue.

uniqueFindings.title: Expired pending bid remains active and keeps funds reserved
uniqueFindings.summary: after the exact scenario-owned bid passed its seeded near-boundary expiry and the Investor refreshed the rendered application, it still appeared as one active Pending offer. The wallet remained USD 4,800 current and USD 4,550 available, leaving the bid's USD 250 reservation held. Expected: once a pending bid reaches its expiry, refresh/reopen moves it out of active offers, records an auditable expired terminal state, and releases the reservation exactly once. Impact: expired offers remain actionable-looking and strand customer funds, directly blocking reuse or withdrawal of the reserved amount.

uniqueFindings.title: Pitch preference state is contradictory and Favourites filtering is inaccurate
uniqueFindings.summary: selecting Dislike while Like was active produced both Unlike pitch and Remove dislike, and a full refresh preserved both reactions. After both reactions were removed and a re-login showed neutral controls, selecting Favourites displayed the complete 33-pitch directory instead of an empty favourite set. Expected: Like and Dislike are mutually exclusive; the active Favourites filter contains only pitches the Investor has favourited/liked and shows an honest empty state after removal. Impact: preference signals can contradict each other and the saved-items directory cannot be trusted for discovery or cleanup.

uniqueFindings.title: Follow and unfollow totals remain stale until identity handoff
uniqueFindings.summary: Follow persisted as Unfollow after refresh while the target still showed zero followers. After a later identity handoff the target showed one. Unfollow then persisted as Follow after refresh while the target still showed one; only signing in again as the target reconciled the dashboard to zero. Expected: after Follow or Unfollow succeeds, the target's displayed follower total changes atomically with the persisted action state and stays correct after refresh. Impact: public social proof and owner summaries are visibly wrong during the active session, so users cannot reliably verify whether the mutation reconciled.

uniqueFindings.title: Successful profile report renders a blank acknowledgement toast
uniqueFindings.summary: after Submit closed the dialog, the application rendered a toast containing only its close icon and no message. Admin later confirmed exactly one report with the submitted target, reporter and details. Expected: profile-report submission provides a visible, meaningful success or failure acknowledgement so the reporter knows whether to retry. Impact: the reporter receives no usable confirmation and may retry or contact support despite a successful moderation-side write.

uniqueFindings.title: Investor project wallet falsely displays zero balance and no ledger
uniqueFindings.summary: each of two accepted shareholders saw USD 0 current/available and an empty project transaction table. The owner of the same project saw USD 945 current/available plus successful USD 1,000 project-funding and USD 55 dividend-payout rows. Expected: an authorized project shareholder can reconcile the project's funded wallet and relevant project ledger against the same project state visible to its owner, subject to documented privacy rules. Impact: both Investors receive a materially false project financial state and cannot reconcile funding or returns. No asset loss or unauthorized transaction was proved, so this is High rather than Critical.

uniqueFindings.title: Project Equity omits other CIC shareholders and contradicts funded ownership
uniqueFindings.summary: the 2% shareholder saw own 2% and Other CIC 0%; the 8% shareholder saw own 8% and Other CIC 0%; an unrelated Investor's aggregate view showed CIC 0% and Unallocated 100%. The same project header reported 10% on CIC and two investors. Expected: each authorized viewer sees an internally consistent aggregate capitalization view for the project; the combined CIC percentage reconciles to accepted bids and the project header, while any actor-specific breakdown follows documented privacy rules. Impact: ownership displayed to Investors does not reconcile to the accepted investment state, creating material cap-table and governance uncertainty.

uniqueFindings.title: Owner cannot create a milestone using selectable valid dates
uniqueFindings.summary: the owner selected September 12, September 10 and September 11 in separate attempts. Each date rendered in the field, but submission returned Milestone achieved date is required and must be valid; no milestone was created. The future date was correctly disabled, and empty/whitespace title validation worked. Expected: after required text is supplied, a current or earlier selectable achieved date creates exactly one completed milestone and survives refresh. Impact: the owner cannot record a completed delivery through the rendered product, blocking milestone-driven reporting and Investor review.

uniqueFindings.title: Milestone comment validation and Unicode recovery silently lose input
uniqueFindings.summary: whitespace closed the dialog with no visible error and created nothing. A valid unique Unicode clarification remained indefinitely in loading and disappeared after reload with zero comments. A later plain-ASCII comment did persist, narrowing the failure to validation/internationalised-input handling rather than all comments. Expected: whitespace is rejected with actionable validation; valid Unicode text submits exactly once or fails recoverably while retaining input; successful comments persist after reload. Impact: Investors can lose substantive internationalised milestone feedback without a deterministic acknowledgement or recoverable draft. ASCII is a workaround for the observed input, so severity is Medium.

uniqueFindings.title: Owner and unrelated Investor can mutate milestone review state
uniqueFindings.summary: the owner increased the owner's own Alpha milestone from one to two upvotes. An owned Investor whose Project Holdings list contains no project opened the explicit milestone authorization-test URL, received Support/Push back/Add comment controls, incremented Alpha, and posted a comment that persisted after reload. Signed-out access correctly returned to Login. Expected: project owners cannot vote on their own delivery, and an Investor with no holding or other project relationship cannot create reactions or discussion records on that project's milestones. Impact: unaffiliated users can alter project delivery feedback and owners can inflate approval signals. This is High, not Critical, because this run did not prove a payout, formal acceptance threshold, ownership change or irreversible financial effect.

uniqueFindings.title: Required milestone delivery and acceptance lifecycle is absent
uniqueFindings.summary: rendered owner and Investor milestone surfaces exposed only a retrospective Completed milestone title, description and achieved date plus Support, Push back and discussion. No planned/submitted status, progress, evidence, decision or rework control was available. Expected: the project workflow exposes planned/active/late/submitted milestones, progress and delivery evidence, Investor accept/reject/rework decisions, revision history and an auditable terminal state. Impact: the core delivery-review contract in INV-025 cannot be executed, and support/pushback cannot substitute for formal acceptance or rework.

uniqueFindings.title: Valid project RFI submission is silently lost
uniqueFindings.summary: the shareholder entered a unique title, valid Unicode description and a visible September 14 due date. Selecting Request closed the dialog as if successful, but no row, confirmation, error or recoverable draft appeared; the list and count remained unchanged after a real reload. Expected: a valid categorized project information request submitted by an authorized shareholder creates exactly one visible request, confirms success or provides recoverable failure, retains its due date/body and survives reload. Impact: an Investor can believe a due-diligence request was lodged when no accessible record exists, blocking accountability and downstream response while losing entered content.

uniqueFindings.title: Project RFI follow-up, acknowledgment and reopen lifecycle is absent
uniqueFindings.summary: the co-owner's first response automatically changed the request from Open to Closed. Both co-owner and requesting-Investor detail exposed the original description, one Response section and Back only. No category, follow-up, acknowledgment, rework, manual close, reopen, revision history or audit trail was rendered. Expected: after a project owner responds, the requesting Investor can review the ordered private thread, acknowledge or follow up, explicitly close or request rework, and reopen according to policy; both parties can inspect category, revisions, actors and audit timestamps. Impact: one unilateral response terminates the information-request workflow without Investor acceptance, clarification or rework, so the product cannot evidence that due diligence was satisfactorily resolved.

uniqueFindings.title: Whitespace-only project RFI response closes and persists blank
uniqueFindings.summary: the form rejected a truly empty value but accepted spaces only. Selecting Respond closed the dialog, changed the isolated RFI to Closed and rendered an empty Response section. A real reload and requesting-Investor identity handoff preserved the Closed/blank state. Expected: response content is trimmed; empty or whitespace-only input is rejected without changing status, and only a substantive persisted response can advance or close a request. Impact: a responder can falsely mark an Investor due-diligence request resolved without providing information, undermining workflow and audit integrity.

uniqueFindings.title: Required governance-report obligation, review and revision lifecycle is absent
uniqueFindings.summary: the owner surface exposed Drafts, History, Trends and Open Questions with Save as Draft and Submit Report. The Investor surface exposed History, Trends, Open Questions and Ask a Question. A v1 report could be read, questioned, replied to and closed, but neither role exposed a due/late obligation, acknowledgement/acceptance, request-correction/rework, create/compare revision, change/audit history, report export or post-close reopen control. Expected: project reporting exposes due and overdue obligations, draft/submitted/revised states, Investor acknowledgement or acceptance, correction/rework, immutable revision comparison and audit history, export, and a recoverable reopen path after closure. Impact: the available discussion path cannot prove that a report was due on time, formally accepted, corrected or superseded. Governance accountability and immutable review completion therefore remain unverifiable.
